articles.name: Announcing multi-branch steps in action builder
articles.title: Announcing multi-branch steps in action builder
articles.body:
Zendesk is excited to announce support for multiple branches in the branch step in action builder.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

The branch step now supports multiple conditional branches within a single step. Previously, a branch step could only split an action flow into two paths: an If branch and an Else branch. With this update, you can add multiple If branches to one branch step, each with its own condition, allowing a single step to route a flow down many different paths.

With this release, you can:

  • Add up to 20 total branches: Configure up to 19 If branches alongside one default Else branch in a single Branch step.

  • Manage individual branches: Edit, rename, and delete If branches as needed. The Else branch cannot be edited or assigned a condition; it serves as the default fallback path when none of the If conditions are met.

  • Control evaluation order: Reorder branches directly on the branch configuration screen. Conditions are evaluated from left to right, and the first condition that evaluates to true executes its branch.

  • Use familiar condition logic: Build branch conditions using the same condition builder interface already available in the Branch step.

Your existing flows are not affected. Existing branch steps using the original two-path setup continue to run as they do today. When you add a new branch step to a flow, it automatically uses the multi-branch version.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Real-world workflows frequently require routing based on more than two outcomes, such as language, region, request type, or customer tier. Previously, handling multiple outcomes required nesting multiple branch steps inside one another, making flows harder to build, read, and maintain. Supporting multiple branches in a single step simplifies flow architecture and makes complex routing logic much easier to manage.

What do I need to do?

No action is required to enable this feature. The updated branch step will be available automatically for all eligible Suite and Support plans with access to action builder.

  • Existing steps: Continue working without interruption. To upgrade an existing two-path branch step to the multi-branch version, manually replace the step in your flow.

  • New steps: Any new branch step added to a flow will use the multi-branch version by default.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Service Incident - November 3, 2026 - AI Agents | AI agents are unresponsive
articles.title: Service Incident - November 3, 2026 - AI Agents | AI agents are unresponsive
articles.body:
Summary

On November 3, 2026 from 10:20 to 15:30 UTC AI Agents customers across all pods experienced AI Agents failures, including fallback answers, generic technical reply errors, failed handoffs to human agents, failing actions, and dashboard pages failing to load.

Timeline

November 3, 2026 10:20 UTC | November 3, 2026 02:20 PST

We began receiving alerts from multiple pods, followed by customer tickets reporting issues accessing AI Agents dashboards and end-user messages sent as technical errors.

November 3, 2026 10:58 UTC | November 3, 2026 02:58 PST
We’re investigating an issue affecting AI Agents. Customers may receive fallback responses instead of answers, be unable to escalate conversations to a human agent, or have trouble loading the AI Agents dashboard. Our engineering team is working to identify the cause. We don’t yet have an estimated recovery time, but we’ll share updates as more information becomes available.

November 3, 2026 11:46 UTC | November 3, 2026 03:46 PST
We’re continuing our recovery efforts for the AI Agents issue. A staged redeployment is in progress, and we’re monitoring its impact across affected services. While this work is underway, some customers may continue to experience the issue. We’re also investigating cases where the problem persists and validating the service before confirming recovery. At this time, we can’t confirm that service has fully recovered or provide an estimated resolution time. We’ll continue to share updates as we learn more.

November 3, 2026 13:05 UTC | November 3, 2026 05:05 PST
We’re seeing signs of improvement following service restarts, but some customers may still have issues with AI Agents responding, handing conversations off to a human agent, or loading the dashboard. Our engineering team is restarting additional affected services and investigating the remaining errors. We apologize for the continued disruption and will share another update as recovery progresses.

November 3, 2026 15:46 UTC |  November 3, 2026 05:46 PST
We’ve identified an additional change needed to restore AI Agents. Our engineering team is working on the change and testing the service. We’re sorry for the continued disruption. We’ll share another update as soon as we have more information.

November 3, 2026 16:20 UTC | November 3, 2026 PST
Our team's recent changes are showing promising improvement in the issue affecting AI Agents services. EU customers may see this improvement already, and we are moving to roll out to US customers momentarily to mitigate impact. Thank you for your continued patience as we work to address the issues seen today.

November 3, 2026 16:53 UTC | November 3, 2026 06:53 PST
We are seeing improvement for most customers affected by the AI Agents issues, but there are some lingering symptoms as the fix finishes rolling out and system function is restored. Our team is monitoring to ensure that all functionality has improved, and we will provide further updates as we approach full recovery.

November 3, 2026 17:42 UTC | November 3, 2026 07:42 PST
We are happy to report that the issues affecting AI Agents have been resolved, and bot conversations and other affected functionality should be restored at this time. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.

Root Cause Analysis

During an unscheduled secret rotation, the updated secret did not propagate to all services correctly. This caused AI Agent services to be unable to sign and validate tokens for service-to-service communication and led to disrupted agent workflows: AI Agents entered fallback behavior, and instead sent technical error replies, and could not escalate. Additionally as a result of this communication failure, AI Agent dashboards also became stuck in a refresh loop and could not be loaded.

Resolution

We corrected the issue by redeploying and applying the missing secrets across all impacted services. Once this was complete, error rates and product behavior returned to normal across products and features in all pods by 15:15 UTC. Due to the nature of our infrastructure partitioning some customers may have experienced earlier recovery.

We performed an audit of our outcome based pricing engine during the incident and we can confirm there were no observed miscounting of resolutions during the incident. If you have further questions on usage billing during this incident please reach out to your Zendesk representative.

Remediation Items

  1. Review and reinforce deployment and monitoring standards: including unscheduled secret rotations.
  2. Production and pre-production monitor review: to identify and implement improvements to proactively identify similar token propagation failures.
  3. Review and update playbook for AI agents workarounds: to effectively communicate verified mitigation steps we can recommend during similar incidents.
  4. Analyze outcome based pricing engine for any billing inaccuracies: We observed no inaccurate usage charges during our review of this incident.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Announcing the general availability of PDF ingestion for knowledge connectors
articles.title: Announcing the general availability of PDF ingestion for knowledge connectors
articles.body:
We're excited to announce the general availability of PDF ingestion. When you connect SharePoint, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, Zendesk, or Amazon S3 as a knowledge source, PDFs stored there are now brought into Zendesk automatically. That content is available wherever external content is used.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

PDF ingestion is now generally available for the SharePoint, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, Zendesk, and Amazon S3 knowledge connectors. It was previously offered as an Early Access Program (EAP). When these connectors sync, Zendesk extracts the text from your PDFs and makes it available to AI agents, Copilot, search, and generative search.

The following limits apply when ingesting PDF content for use as an external knowledge source:

  • Maximum PDF file size: 20 MB
  • Maximum number of PDFs per account:
    • Team: 100
    • Growth & Professional: 500
    • Enterprise: 1000

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Many organizations keep critical knowledge in PDFs, such as product manuals, policies, and guides. With PDF ingestion generally available, AI agents, Copilot, and generative search can use that knowledge to give your customers and agents faster, more accurate answers. You don't need to convert or migrate the files yourself.

What do I need to do?

PDF ingestion is generally available to customers who have Knowledge as part of their Zendesk subscription and use the SharePoint or Google Drive connector.

  • If you joined the EAP: No action is needed. PDFs you've already ingested remain available, and you no longer need to be enrolled in the EAP.
  • If you didn't join the EAP: ingestion is turned on automatically for supported connections. Your PDFs are ingested on the next sync. See Connecting external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Error: AADSTS650056 appears when signing in to Zendesk
articles.title: Error: AADSTS650056 appears when signing in to Zendesk
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When I try to sign in to Zendesk using single sign-on (SSO) with Microsoft Entra, I see the error:

AADSTS650056: Misconfigured application. This could be due to one of the following: the client has not listed any permissions for 'AAD Graph' in the requested permissions in the client's application registration. Or, the admin has not consented in the tenant. Or, check the application identifier in the request to ensure it matches the configured client application identifier. Or, check the certificate in the request to ensure it's valid. Please contact your admin to fix the configuration or consent on behalf of the tenant. Client app ID: xxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxx.

Root cause

Microsoft Entra ID, not Zendesk, returns the error AADSTS650056: Misconfigured application before the user authenticates. It usually means the Issuer in the Zendesk SAML request doesn't match the Identifier (Entity ID) configured in the Entra enterprise application.

Zendesk sends the Issuer as <subdomain>.zendesk.com, so the Entra value must use a format Entra accepts.

Resolution steps

The most common mistake is the https:// prefix. In most cases, https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com fails where <subdomain>.zendesk.com works. If the error occurs, test both formats in the Entra Identifier (Entity ID) field, with and without https://, and save after each change.

For more information, see Error AADSTS650056: Misconfigured application.

articles.name: When can I reshare a ticket after unsharing?
articles.title: When can I reshare a ticket after unsharing?
articles.body:
Question

I have a ticket shared with another Zendesk account. I want to unshare the ticket and then share it again. How long do I need to wait before resharing?

Answer

Wait at least 1 to 2 minutes after unsharing a ticket before you share it again. This makes sure the ticket appears in the partner account right away.

You don't have to wait. But if you reshare too soon, one of the following can happen:

  • Within the first few seconds of unsharing: the unshare may not have finished processing on the partner account's side. The share may not reach the partner account correctly, and the ticket may not appear.
  • Within about 60 seconds of unsharing: the ticket may take several minutes to appear in the partner account.

For more information, see Sharing and unsharing tickets.

articles.name: Release notes through 2026-11-06
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-11-06
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of last month's releases.

This week's release notes include:

  • Knowledge
  • AI Agents
  • AI/Copilot
  • App Marketplace
  • Products with no updates this week

Knowledge

New

  • Knowledge Graph
    • Connectors are now available for Gong, Shopify, Dynamics 365, Zammad, and Linear.
    • Suggested actions in the Knowledge panel now remain available for the rest of your session. You can refresh them, expand or collapse them, and they respect your viewing history for linked articles and posts.
    • The Universal Connector setup now displays a banner if AI mapping doesn't suggest any data mappings. The connection form also checks that you've selected an authentication method before you continue.

Fixed

  • Knowledge
    • Content from Contentful no longer intermittently disappears from Help Center search results.
    • The Contentful connector no longer syncs draft content types.
    • Jira connections no longer show a misleading syncing status.
    • Quick answers in the Knowledge sidebar app now appear in the user's language instead of English.
    • Articles opened from citations now display correctly in the Knowledge panel.
    • You can no longer enable more than five suggested questions for a locale. The suggested questions page is also more accessible with a keyboard and screen readers.
  • Procedures
    • Procedure version history now shows unpublished events.
  • Article Editor
    • Inserting a callout no longer disrupts list items or numbering.
    • The correct empty state now appears when suggested changes can't be anchored.
    • Archiving an article in recommendation mode now takes you to the archived view.
    • Selecting Update article for a recommendation on a secondary brand now opens the correct brand.
    • API articles are no longer incorrectly marked as legacy.
    • Accepting an AI translation now republishes an already-published translation when needed.
  • Help Center
    • The updated Copenhagen theme now loads locale-specific translations before falling back to the base language. Install v4.53.6 to get the fix.
    • Help Center search and community posts now have improved heading structure, image alternative text, and link distinction for people using screen readers or a keyboard.

AI Agents

New

  • AI Agents Insights
    • The AI agent launchpad is a guided experience that speeds up setup, helps you get value sooner, and supports performance improvements across AI agents. The rollout starts November 5 and ends November 30. See Using the agent overview to monitor and manage a specific AI agent.

AI/Copilot

New

  • Create custom summaries for tickets and calls
  • You can now specify brands, groups, and ticket tags to control when auto assist considers each procedure. See  Creating procedures for auto assist.
  • Auto assist now filters internal notes before using them. This lets it use private team context to help resolve tickets without exposing sensitive information to end users.
  • AI Translations
    • The AI translations glossary is generally available to all customers with the Copilot add-on, giving you control over how AI-generated translations handle your business-specific terminology.
    • Messaging translations are now saved: Translated agent replies in messaging channels are saved and shown again in Agent Workspace. Agents don't have to wait for a conversation to be translated again when they return to it. Another agent can also view and translate the conversation.

Fixed

  • Auto assist no longer regenerates plans unnecessarily when internal triggers update. It also now parses media without captions and file attachments into ticket context, helping prevent it from over- or underreacting.
  • Auto assist now retains customer details, such as names and email addresses, submitted through bot forms. Agents don't have to ask customers to repeat information they've already provided.
  • Auto assist no longer removes key customer details from forwarded emails in a ticket's opening message.
  • Auto assist now copies procedure IDs correctly, preventing incorrect suggestions.
  • You can now use View related tickets for IT trigger recommendations to see the tickets associated with each recommendation.
  • Accepted topic suggestions now appear in the topic list even when their categories or subcategories are under review, and tickets are classified with those topics.

App Marketplace

New

  • Zengine WhatsApp Channel
    • Zengine WhatsApp Channel connects WhatsApp conversations to Zendesk, so agents can handle them alongside other support channels. Teams can use it to design, manage, and measure customer conversations.
  • Holiday Manager
    • Holiday Manager helps administrators update business hours schedules for public holidays in more than 100 countries. Admins can choose a schedule and region, review holidays, and upload them to keep SLA calendars current.
  • Dynamic Content Manager
    • Dynamic Content Manager provides a full-page workspace for managing multilingual Zendesk dynamic content. Admins can search names, placeholders, and variant text, then filter items by type.
  • Heedwell: Public Reply Guard
    • Heedwell checks public replies for mistakes, such as internal notes sent publicly, references to another customer, and unfinished placeholders. It helps agents catch risky or incomplete messages before they reach customers.
  • Everytide: Recurring Tickets
    • Everytide creates recurring tickets on a calendar so teams can schedule routine work, such as audits and maintenance. Teams can configure when tickets recur instead of creating each one manually.
  • Tomewell: Help Center PDF Manuals
    • Tomewell turns help center content into branded PDF manuals for different brands and languages. Teams can rebuild manuals after content changes, giving customers and partners an up-to-date offline guide.
  • Twigwell: Split Tickets
    • Twigwell separates a distinct request from an existing ticket by moving selected comments into a new ticket. It helps agents keep unrelated conversations and follow-ups organized while preserving their context.
  • Hourwell: Custom Timers and OLAs
    • Hourwell tracks working time based on ticket conditions, such as group, status, assignee, fields, or tags. It alerts teams as a goal approaches or is missed, helping them manage deadlines between teams.
  • Sprucewell: Help Center Find, Replace and Links
    • Sprucewell finds text and links across help center articles and languages, so teams can update product names and fix broken links from one workspace. It supports 301 redirects to preserve old addresses after a change.
  • Hitchwell: ClickUp Tasks from Tickets
    • Hitchwell creates a ClickUp task from a Zendesk ticket and attaches the conversation. Linked tasks appear in the ticket sidebar with their status, assignees, due dates, priorities, and latest comments.

articles.name: Performing A/B testing on generative procedures
articles.title: Performing A/B testing on generative procedures
articles.body:
A/B testing allows you to compare a livegenerative procedurewith an updated draft version of the same procedure using real customer conversations. It compares their automated resolution rate to determine whether the draft version performs better than the live version. This helps you decide whether to publish your updated procedure or keep the existing version.

What's my plan?

Summary: ◀▼

Use A/B testing to compare a live generative procedure with one draft variant in real customer conversations and see whether the draft improves automated resolution rates. Admins can set traffic splits and test duration, review results and conversation metrics, and publish a winning variant. Tests can be canceled at any time; outcomes are a variant win or inconclusive.

A/B testing allows you to compare a live generative procedure with an updated draft version of the same procedure using real customer conversations. It compares their automated resolution rate to determine whether the draft version performs better than the live version. This helps you decide whether to publish your updated procedure or keep the existing version.

You must be an admin to use A/B testing.

This article contains the following topics:

  • About A/B testing
  • Creating an A/B test
  • Canceling an ongoing A/B test
  • Viewing A/B test results

About A/B testing

A/B testing compares two versions of a generative procedure to determine which performs better:

  • Control: The live procedure currently used by your AI agent.
  • Variant: A draft version of the same procedure that contains changes you want to test against the control.

The test uses real customer conversations to compare the automated resolution rates of the live procedure (control) and draft version (variant) to determine whether the variant performs better at resolving customer requests without intervention from a human agent.

Limitations of A/B testing

A/B testing currently has the following limitations:

  • Automated resolution rate is the only evaluation metric: You can evaluate test performance based on the automated resolution rate only.
  • One-sided testing: The test determines only whether the variant outperforms the control. Possible outcomes indicate whether the variant wins, or the result is inconclusive. It cannot declare the control as the winner.
  • One variant per test: You can test only one draft procedure against the live procedure at a time.

Creating an A/B test

Admins can create an A/B test in the AI agents workspace.

To create an A/B test

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Test in the sidebar, then select A/B tests.
  3. In the top-right corner, click + New A/B test.
  4. Enter a Name and Description of your test.

  5. Select a procedure from the list to use as the Control.
  6. Select a version of the same procedure to use as the Variant.
  7. (Optional) Next to the control and variant, update the percent of customer conversations that should be directed to each procedure version. By default, the traffic split is set to 50/50, but you can assign more traffic to the control for a more conservative test.
  8. Select either of the following durations:
    • Conversation count: The test runs for up to 375 conversations.
    • Fixed duration: Set a start date and end date for the test.
  9. Click Start A/B test to begin testing.

Canceling an ongoing A/B test

You can cancel an A/B test at any time before it reaches its configured end condition.

To cancel an A/B test

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Test in the sidebar, then select A/B tests.
  3. In the top-right, click the options menu and select End experiment.

Once you cancel an A/B test, the test ends immediately, and no winner is declared. But you can still access the canceled test and view the metrics collected before cancellation for reference.

Viewing A/B test results

While an A/B test is ongoing and after it’s complete, you can view its results to compare the performance of the control and variant.

To view A/B test results

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Test in the sidebar, then select A/B tests.
  3. Select the ongoing or completed A/B test you want to review.

The dashboard displays the following metrics:

  • Traffic split: A pie chart showing the total number of conversations that use the control or the variant.
  • BSAT score: The percentage of customers who rate the AI agent 4 or 5 after their conversation. It is calculated by dividing the number of ratings of 4 or 5 by the total number of ratings received, and multiplying by 100.
  • Automated resolutions rate: The percentage of eligible conversations that end with a verified resolution.
  • Automated resolutions (AR) over time: A time-series view of the AR over the duration of the experiment.
  • Assisted escalations rate: The percentage of eligible conversations in which the AI agent helped the customer before handing the conversation to a human agent.
  • Assisted escalations over time: A time-series view of the assisted escalation rate over the duration of the experiment.

Understanding A/B test outcomes

A completed A/B test can have one of the following outcomes:

  • Variant wins: The draft version achieved a statistically significantly higher automated resolution rate than the live version. You can optionally publish the winning variant by clicking View and publish from the test results.
  • Inconclusive: The test could not confirm that the draft version performs better than the live procedure because the difference in automated resolution rates was not statistically significant.

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I create an A/B test for a generative procedure?

You must be an admin. In the AI agents workspace, select an AI agent, go to Test > A/B tests, and click + New A/B test. Name and describe the test, choose the live procedure as the control and a draft version of that same procedure as the variant, set the test duration, and click Start A/B test.

What traffic split and duration can I choose for my A/B test?

The default traffic split is 50/50, and you can adjust the percentages to send more conversations to the control for a more conservative test. You can run the test for a specified conversation count, for which a recommended count is provided based on the split and control’s automated resolution rate, or set a fixed start and end date.

What are the limitations of my A/B test?

Automated resolution rate is the only metric used to evaluate performance. A test can compare only one draft variant with the live control, and it can determine whether the variant wins or the result is inconclusive; it cannot declare the control the winner.

How do I cancel an ongoing A/B test, and what happens afterward?

In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent, go to Test > A/B tests, open the options menu, and select End experiment. The test ends immediately with no winner declared. You can still access it and review metrics collected before cancellation.

How can I review my A/B test results and determine whether I can publish the variant?

In Test > A/B tests, select an ongoing or completed test. The dashboard shows the traffic split, BSAT score, automated resolution rate and its trend, and assisted escalation rate and its trend. You can click View conversations to inspect included conversations. A completed test reports either Variant wins—meaning the variant’s automated resolution rate was statistically significantly higher—or Inconclusive. If the variant wins, you can optionally publish it with View and publish.

articles.name: How can I keep specific use cases on repeated questions in AI agents?
articles.title: How can I keep specific use cases on repeated questions in AI agents?
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I want repeated questions on a specific topic, such as legal or compliance, to enter the same strict, dialogue-driven use case every time. After the use case completes, an immediate follow-up on the same topic goes to clarification, a knowledge search, or a generative reply instead of re-entering the use case.

Root cause

This is intended behavior designed to prevent conversation loops. An AI agent can't select the same use case twice in a row, so the system doesn't guarantee immediate re-entry into a use case. In addition, there's a limit on how many times a conversation can loop through the same block in a dialogue. If the flow passes through the same block three times (for example, if you've linked back to earlier blocks), the AI agent stops attempting to generate a response.

  • After a use case finishes, the AI agent routes a follow-up that would map to the same use case elsewhere, such as a clarification or knowledge search. After another step has run, the agent can select the use case again.
  • The restriction applies to the selection of a use case. If you link from one dialogue to a use case, no selection takes place. The agent still treats the original use case as the last one selected. Linking back to a use case or to the welcome reply is therefore not a reliable way around the restriction.

Resolution steps

No setting guarantees that an AI agent can enter a use case twice in a row. As a workaround, end the use case by linking back to the welcome reply, and have the welcome reply route to the use case through intent detection.

To set up this workaround:

  1. Open the AI agent and edit the use case that must repeat
  2. At the end of its dialogue, add a step that links to the Welcome reply
  3. In the welcome reply, add a Customer message block with an Intent predicted branch for that topic and link it to the use case
  4. Publish your changes and test with consecutive questions on the topic, for example, two order update questions back-to-back, to confirm the use case runs each time

For more information, see Customizing the welcome reply in AI agent conversations.

Notes

  • Zendesk doesn't guarantee this behavior. Test it in your own environment, and re-test after you change your flows.
  • This workaround works around the loop-prevention restriction, which you can't turn off. The agent doesn't select the same use case twice in a row. Because a link isn't a selection, the agent can still treat the original use case as the last one selected. That is why the intent-detection branches matter, and why linking to the welcome reply with no branches may be inconsistent.

Summary

Between 23:25 UTC on 28 October 2026 and 00:35 UTC on 29 October 2026, some users connecting from Mexico were unable to access or sign in to Zendesk Support. Users may have seen an error page or experienced a connection timeout while trying to connect.

Timeline

October 29, 2026 00:28 UTC | October 28, 2026 05:28 PM PT

October 29, 2026 01:26 UTC | October 28, 2026 06:26 PM PT

articles.name: I cannot get my AI agent to follow instructions
articles.title: I cannot get my AI agent to follow instructions
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I need your help with an issue with AI agent instructions. In particular, I'm trying to get my AI agent to provide the exact full title of the relevant help article, along with a one-sentence description of how it helps. I'm instructing my AI agent to do so with this sample sentence: "When answering from help center content, list each relevant article using its exact full title from the metadata, in quotation marks. After each title, add one concise sentence that explains how the article helps." However, the AI agent still fails to do this on the first response. When the user asks a follow-up question, the AI agent suddenly nails the exact format I want.

Do you know of any instruction tweaks or backend settings I can apply so it gets the format right on the first try?

Root cause

While instructions are a good way to try to influence the AI agent response, the non-deterministic nature of AI can make very specific instructions unreliable.

Instructions can influence this format, but they can't guarantee it.

Why the first reply may differ from the follow-up

The system applies instructions after it generates the answer. They "shape, but not fundamentally change" the response, as the article Using instructions to influence AI agent responses explains. The same pattern occurs in other cases with similar formatting issues.

Resolution steps

Make the instruction more explicit and positive

For example: "In every reply that uses help center content, end with a section called 'Related articles:' that lists each article's exact title, copied verbatim from the article metadata, in quotation marks. After each title, add one concise sentence explaining how it helps." Avoid conditional wording such as "when relevant."

Use a procedure if you need it on every first reply

Put the requirement in a procedure that always includes the titles. This worked as a workaround for the missing-links case.

Use the widget's citation display if the goal is visible, clickable titles

The messaging Web Widget has a messageLog.citations.sources setting with the options 'button', 'bulletedList', and 'numberedList'. The list options show the sources directly under the message and don't depend on the large language model (LLM) following an instruction.

articles.title: Analyzing the quality of AI agent conversations
articles.body:
In the AI agents workspace, the Evaluation dashboard helps you understand the quality of the conversations your AI agents are having with customers. This dashboard uses automated evaluations to highlight where your AI agents understand customer needs and provide relevant answers, and where interactions need attention.

Summary: ◀▼

Use the Evaluation dashboard to review automated, post-conversation assessments of your AI agent’s comprehension, empathy, repetition, and customer escalation requests. Track these measures over time and compare results by AI agent, topic, channel, language, or reply type to identify conversations that may need attention. Evaluations aren’t live, and the dashboard doesn’t provide custom scorecards or a single overall quality score.

In the AI agents workspace, the Evaluation dashboard helps you understand the quality of the conversations your AI agents are having with customers. This dashboard uses automated evaluations to highlight where your AI agents understand customer needs and provide relevant answers, and where interactions need attention.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Important considerations
  • Accessing the Evaluation dashboard
  • Understanding the Evaluation reports

Related articles:

  • Analyzing overall AI agent performance
  • Analyzing use case and knowledge source performance in AI agents
  • Analyzing the conversation journey in AI agents
  • Analyzing custom resolutions in AI agents

Important considerations

Consider the following when using the Evaluation dashboard:

  • Evaluations take place after a conversation ends. This release does not provide live monitoring or alerts during an active conversation.
  • Each category measures a different aspect of the interaction. Comprehension does not mean the issue was resolved.
  • QA comprehension is different from the existing Understood conversations metric, which reflects recorded conversation activity. The two measures can produce different results.
  • Requested escalation is different from assisted escalation: a request to speak to a human does not establish that a handover succeeded or that the issue was resolved.
  • Not every category applies to every conversation. Missing, not-applicable, or failed evaluations are not negative quality results.
  • The initial release uses predefined evaluation criteria. It does not include custom scorecards or a single overall AI agent quality score.

Accessing the Evaluation dashboard

The Evaluation dashboard is available in Analytics.

To access the dashboard

  • In Analytics, click AI agents then click the Evaluation tab.

Understanding the Evaluation reports

The Evaluation dashboard uses automated evaluations to assess eligible AI agent conversations after they end, across the following categories:

  • Comprehension rate: Whether the AI agent demonstrated an accurate understanding of the customer’s issue through its summary of the issue, targeted questions, or a fitting solution.
  • Empathy score: Whether the AI agent acknowledged the customer’s emotions or frustrations and validated their concerns.
  • Escalation request rate: Whether the customer asked to speak to a human, accepted the bot-offered handoff, or commented about escalating to an outside entity.
  • Repetition rate: Whether the AI agent repeated the same requests, instructions, or fallback responses without meaningful progress.

The Evaluation dashboard includes the following reports:

  • Evaluation over time:
    • % Comprehension rate: The percentage of conversations where the AI agent correctly understood the customer’s issue. Evaluated as yes or no.
    • % Empathy score: The percentage of conversations where the bot acknowledged customer emotions or frustrations and validated their concerns.
    • % Repetition rate: The percentage of conversations where the bot repeated the same fallback, request, or instruction across multiple turns without meaningful progress or new information.
    • % Escalation request rate: The percentage of conversations where the customer explicitly asked for escalation or requests another team.
  • Evaluation by AI agent and topic:
    • Checkbox: Check to select all listed agents.
    • AI agent name: The AI agent being evaluated.
    • Conversation topics: Topics covered in the conversation.
    • Conversations: Total conversations conducted by the agent.
    • Comprehension rate: The percentage of conversations where the AI agent correctly understood the customer’s issue.
    • Empathy score: The percentage of conversations with a positive empathy score.
    • Repetition rate: The percentage of conversations where the bot repeated the same fallback, request, or instruction across multiple turns without meaningful progress or new information.

At the bottom of the dashboard, you can view reports for each evaluation category filtered by:

  • AI agent name
  • Conversation channel
  • Conversation language
  • Conversation reply type
  • Conversation topics

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I access the AI agent Evaluation dashboard?

In Analytics, click AI agents, then click the Evaluation tab.

What does the Evaluation dashboard measure about my AI agent conversations?

After eligible conversations end, it evaluates comprehension (whether the agent understood the issue), empathy (whether it acknowledged and validated emotions or concerns), escalation requests, and repetition without meaningful progress.

What reports and filters can I use to analyze evaluation results?

The dashboard provides Evaluation over time and Evaluation by AI agent and topic reports. Reports for each evaluation category can be filtered by AI agent name, conversation channel, language, reply type, and topic.

Can I monitor conversations live or create a custom overall quality score?

No. Evaluations happen after conversations end, and this release has no live monitoring or alerts, custom scorecards, or single overall AI agent quality score.

How should I interpret evaluation results that differ from other metrics or are missing?

QA comprehension can differ from the Understood conversations metric. Comprehension does not mean an issue was resolved, and an escalation request does not prove a handover succeeded or the issue was resolved. Missing, not-applicable, or failed evaluations are not negative quality results.

articles.name: Can I remove the "[AI]" Prefix from AI agent WhatsApp Responses?
articles.title: Can I remove the "[AI]" Prefix from AI agent WhatsApp Responses?
articles.body:
Question

Is there a way to turn off the "[AI]" mention or prefix that appears in AI agent responses for the WhatsApp channel?

Answer

Yes. You can remove the "[AI]" prefix in AI agent responses for the WhatsApp channel if you have a developer team. Set showAIDisclaimer to false on the WhatsApp integration using the Sunshine Conversations Update Integration API:

PATCH /v2/apps/{appId}/integrations/{integrationId}

Content-Type: application/json
{
"showAIDisclaimer": false
}

Use the integration ID for the relevant WhatsApp channel. The setting defaults to true. Deactivating it stops the "[AI]" prefix on subsequent responses for that integration.

To learn more about creating a Sunshine Conversations API key, see Using Conversations API keys.

Important: If you set this to false, you're responsible for ensuring your integration complies with any applicable AI regulations in the regions where it operates. In addition, Zendesk doesn't provide support for custom code. Consult your developer team for assistance.

articles.name: Using the agent overview to monitor and manage a specific AI agent
articles.title: Using the agent overview to monitor and manage a specific AI agent
articles.body:
In the AI agents workspace, theAgent overviewpage lets you track your AI agent’s performance and explore next steps for better results. In contrast to thedashboard, which gives you an overall look at all AI agents across your account, the Agent overview page gives you an overall look at a specific AI agent.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Use the Agent overview to monitor a specific AI agent’s performance, review automated resolutions, conversations, and recommendations, and identify ways to improve automation and workflows. Filter insights for the last 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days, check agent status, channels, and tone of voice, and access actions for building and launching your agent.

In the AI agents workspace, the Agent overview page lets you track your AI agent’s performance and explore next steps for better results. In contrast to the dashboard, which gives you an overall look at all AI agents across your account, the Agent overview page gives you an overall look at a specific AI agent.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Accessing the overview for a specific AI agent
  • Understanding the AI agent overview

Accessing the overview for a specific AI agent

You can access the overview for a specific AI agent from the sidebar. For active AI agents, you can also access the overview from the dashboard.
Note: The Agent overview page isn’t available for AI agents with a status of Setup incomplete.

To access the AI agent overview from the sidebar

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Optimize in the sidebar, then select Agent overview.

    The AI agent overview page opens.

Note: Once you’re on the Agent overview page, you can switch between overviews for different AI agents by using the AI agent selector in the top menu bar.

To access the AI agent overview from the dashboard (active AI agents only)

  1. In the AI agents workspace, click Dashboard in the sidebar.
  2. In the list of AI agents, select the active AI agent you want to view.

    The Agent overview page opens.

Understanding the AI agent overview

The Agent overview page includes the following sections:

  • Agent insights
  • Recommendations
  • Agent details
  • Quick actions

You can use the time filter at the top-right of the page to filter the information for the last 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days. You can also click View all analytics to view the Agent performance dashboard.

Agent insights

The Agent insights section shows the following metrics for the selected AI agent:

  • Automated resolutions (AR): The percentage of conversations that result in an automated resolution.
  • Conversations: The total number of conversations between this AI agent and customers.
  • Understood conversations: The percentage and number of conversations where any of the following are true:
    • An answer was provided from a knowledge source.
    • A use case was triggered.
    • The conversation was directly escalated to a human agent without an answer being provided or a use case being triggered.
    Note: For AI agents with agentic AI, this metric excludes small talk and conversations escalated through the Escalation system reply. Because the Escalation system reply is excluded, this metric might be lower compared to other AI agents because manually created use cases for escalations are no longer triggered.

Recommendations

The Recommendations section shows suggested actions you can take to automate manual tasks and optimize workflows for the selected AI agent.

Note: The Recommendations section doesn’t appear for client users.

Recommendations for Voice AI agents are based on text conversation, such as email and messaging, rather than voice conversations.

Click View details to see more about a specific recommendation, or click View all to open the Recommendations page.

Agent details

The Agent details section shows the following information about the selected AI agent:

  • Status: The status of an AI agent, which can be one of the following:
    • Active: The AI agent is currently interacting with customers on the channels it’s connected to. Click Manage to manage the AI agent’s general settings.
    • Ready to activate: The AI agent’s configuration is sufficient to begin interacting with customers, but it isn’t yet live. Click Activate to connect it to the channels it should be available to customers on.
    • Setup incomplete: The Agent overview page isn’t available for AI agents with a status of Setup incomplete.
  • Manage channels: The channel type and number of channels the AI agent is currently connected to. Click Set up channels to connect it to the channels it should be available to customers on.
  • Manage tone of voice: The AI agent’s current tone of voice. Click Manage tone of voice to customize the AI agent’s tone of voice.

Quick actions

The Quick actions section provides access to next steps in the following areas:

  • Build: Personalize your AI agent, fill knowledge gaps, and connect it to actions. Click Go to knowledge sources to connect knowledge sources to your AI agent.
  • Launch: Click Go to launch to manage the channels the AI agent is connected to.

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I open the overview for a specific AI agent, and when is it unavailable?

In the AI agents workspace, select the agent, click Optimize in the sidebar, and choose Agent overview. You can also open it from the Dashboard by selecting an active AI agent. The overview isn’t available for agents with Setup incomplete status. Use the selector in the top menu bar to switch between agents.

What performance metrics can I see for my AI agent, and what counts as an understood conversation?

Agent insights shows the percentage of conversations that result in an automated resolution, the total number of conversations, and the percentage and number of understood conversations. A conversation is understood if an answer came from a knowledge source, a use case was triggered, or it was directly escalated to a human without an answer or use case. Small talk and conversations escalated through the Escalation system reply are excluded, which can make this metric lower than for other agents.

How can I change the date range for my agent overview or see more analytics?

Use the time filter at the top right to view information for the last 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days. Click View all analytics to open the Agent performance dashboard.

What recommendations can I review for my AI agent, and can I access them as a client user?

The Recommendations section suggests actions to automate manual tasks and optimize workflows. Click View details to learn about a recommendation or View all to open the Recommendations page. This section doesn’t appear for client users.

How can I manage my AI agent’s status, channels, tone, and setup next steps from the overview?

In Agent details, an Active agent is interacting with customers on its connected channels; click Manage to adjust its general settings. For an agent that is Ready to activate, click Activate to connect it to customer-facing channels. Setup incomplete agents don’t have an overview. You can click Set up channels to connect channels and Manage tone of voice to customize the agent’s tone. Quick actions also lets you connect knowledge sources through Go to knowledge sources and manage connected channels through Go to launch.

articles.name: Service Incident - October 23, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Zendesk Timing out
articles.title: Service Incident - October 23, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Zendesk Timing out
articles.body:
Summary

Between 15:20 UTC and 18:18 UTC on 23 October 2026, Zendesk services experienced intermittent access issues for customers in the Americas, primarily the eastern United States and South America. During the incident, we received 113 customer reports.

Affected users experienced timeouts, blank pages, error messages, and slower-than-expected page loading. These symptoms disrupted access to Zendesk and could delay ticketing activities and other customer support workflows.

Timeline

October 23, 2026 16:09 UTC | October 23, 2026 09:09 AM PT

Our CDN provider experienced a spike in errors affecting traffic for some customers in US-East between 15:20 and 15:45 UTC, but have significantly improved since that time. We are monitoring the situation to ensure stability; however, some users in that area may still experience degraded traffic and some latency may be expected until they have fully recovered.

October 23, 2026 16:53 UTC | October 23, 2026 09:53 AM PT

Our CDN provider has released a fix and we are seeing recovery in traffic to affected US-East users. Thank you for your patience as we worked to mitigate the impact and restore access.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a network issue at a provider that supports our content delivery service. Multiple network connections failed at the same time, reducing available capacity and causing slower access and intermittent errors for some customers in the Americas.

Resolution

To restore service, our content delivery provider redirected traffic away from the affected network connections. This reduced congestion and returned service to normal. The alternative routing remained in place while the underlying provider repaired the affected connections.

Remediation Items

  1. Update existing security certificates to ensure they include all required validation information.
  2. Review the content delivery provider’s root cause analysis and document any required follow-up actions.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.body:
Click Follow in the What's New section to be notified each month when the What's New is published.

Support

  • Subticket creation and ticket linking for task lists lets agents connect downstream work to the original request by linking existing tickets or creating subtickets from tasks, while tracking assignee, status, and progress from the main ticket. See Creating task lists to help agents solve tickets.

  • The ability to change the brand on closed tickets lets admins update a closed ticket’s brand without reopening it, helping keep historical data, reporting, and audits accurate. See Modifying closed tickets.
  • Parallel approval requests let agents assign one approval request to up to five approvers at once, so all reviewers can respond independently and in any order. The request is approved only when every approver agrees, and any denial withdraws the remaining requests. See Creating approval requests.
  • Agent email attachments can now be enabled alongside secure downloads, letting agents send standard email attachments while oversized files remain protected as authenticated Zendesk-hosted links. See Allowing agents to attach files to emails and Allowing secure downloads.
  • Multiple task lists let agents add up to five distinct task lists to a ticket, using templates or custom lists, with per-list status tracking and subticket support. See Using task lists within tickets.
  • Visual alerts for task lists now appear in the ticket context panel, using a numbered badge to highlight unviewed active task lists as soon as they’re added. See Using task lists within tickets.

  • One-time passcode (OTP) verification lets admins require anonymous recipients to verify their email address before accessing Zendesk-hosted ticket attachments. See Requiring a one-time passcode to access email attachments for details.

AI agents

  • AI agent ticket takeover and editing now lets authorized admins and agents add internal notes, tags, and custom field updates while a conversation is ongoing, and take over the ticket to hand control to a human. See Interacting with AI agent tickets.
  • Generative procedures for AI agents will soon be written in plain language. Procedures are moving from visual procedure maps to plain-language text, with read-only text versions now available and full text editing coming later. No action is required yet. See Previewing a procedure in natural language text.
  • Email attachment recognition now lets AI agents with agentic AI read image and PDF attachments in customer emails, extract relevant details, assess visual content, and use that information to resolve conversations without manual review. See Capabilities of AI agents with agentic AI.
  • AI agent access can now be controlled through custom roles. Admins can set access once for everyone in a role, then manage those permissions from Roles and permissions instead of updating team members individually. See Managing access with custom roles.
  • Navigation in the AI agents workspace has been streamlined. The left sidebar includes tools grouped around your key tasks to support you from your first AI agent launch through ongoing improvements and growth. See Accessing and navigating the AI agents workspace.
  • AI agent use cases can now be used with proactive messages in the Web Widget and mobile SDK channels. When an end user responds to a proactive message, their conversation is automatically routed to the selected AI agent use case. See Creating proactive messages for the Web Widget and Creating proactive messages for mobile SDK channels.

Copilot

  • Procedure testing for auto assist lets admins test unpublished procedures and draft changes directly in the Knowledge admin procedure editor before publishing. Admins can simulate customer conversations, review suggestions and rationale, and refine procedures without creating separate test tickets. See Testing procedures for auto assist.

  • Auto assist can now recognize attachments in ticket comments and messaging tickets, including file names and extensions, improving reply and action suggestions for attachment-dependent workflows. See Attachment recognition in Copilot auto assist.

  • Suggested assignees gives agents ranked recommendations for who should handle a ticket when reassigning or escalating. See Turning on suggested assignees.

  • Copilot similar tickets is now included at no additional cost for Suite and Support Professional plans and above. This feature shows agents recently resolved tickets that match the current case so they can reuse proven solutions faster. See Turning on similar tickets.

  • Custom summaries for tickets and calls let admins define the information, tone, and format AI uses when generating summaries, including tag-based instructions and default settings for unmatched tickets. See Creating custom summaries for tickets and calls.
  • The intelligent triage ticket field migration will move legacy custom ticket fields for topic, language, and sentiment to standard ticket fields. Migrations are scheduled from October 26 through December 4, 2026. Update any workflows using intelligent triage tags to use the corresponding standard fields. See Understanding the intelligent triage ticket field migration.

Objects and business rules

  • AI-built action flows lets you describe automation in plain text and automatically generate editable visual workflows, including triggers, conditions, branches, native actions, and custom API-based actions. See Using AI to create action flows.
  • Action flow testing lets you use recent tickets or sample users to auto-populate test fields, reducing manual ID entry and making action flow validation faster and easier. See Testing an action flow.
  • Action builder now lets admins drag and drop steps to reorder flows, including branches and loops, without deleting and recreating them. Built-in safeguards prevent invalid placements, helping teams refactor automations faster. See Rearranging the steps in an action flow.
  • Action flows now support search, filters, and column sorting in Admin Center, helping admins quickly find specific flows and organize the list more efficiently. See Editing and managing action flows.
  • Action builder supports AND/OR condition logic and two-level condition grouping in workflow triggers, letting teams build more complex routing rules within a single flow. See Action flow steps and actions reference.
  • Custom actions now gets an out-of-the-box OAuth connection to use the Zendesk API, eliminating separate client setup and speeding configuration. All eligible plans receive this update automatically. See Creating custom actions for auto-assist, AI agents, and action flows.
  • Action builder received a new List Ticket Comments action that lets admins retrieve ticket comments in flows without custom actions, webhooks, or API calls. It supports public replies, internal notes, ordering, limits, and comment metadata for downstream automations. See Creating action flows to automate processes across Zendesk and external systems.
  • Email alerts for failed action flows now notify admins when an action flow in Action Builder fails, and recipients can be configured so the right teams receive immediate failure alerts. See Monitoring the usage of action credits and action flow activity.
  • Custom object fields can now be set to allow only unique values, preventing duplicates and letting unique fields serve as external identifiers for finding, updating, or deleting records. Admins can enable this for supported field types on custom objects. See Managing custom objects.
  • Admins can enable anonymous access for a custom object and choose which fields to expose to customers who are not signed in. For example, someone submitting a product complaint can select the products they need help with in the ticket form. See Configuring anonymous access for custom objects.

Accounts and billing

  • Storage usage reporting in Admin Center is being updated to use a more accurate calculation method. Customers may see different usage figures, with historical data visible until November 18, 2026. See Monitoring storage usage in Admin Center.

Security

  • Data masking for ticket comments now lets admins extend masking to names, phone numbers, and email addresses in Support ticket comments, giving more control over what agents can see. Admins can choose whether masking applies to user fields only or also to comments. See Turning on and configuring data masking (ADPP add-on).

People

  • Manage end user configuration is a new custom role permission that lets trusted team members edit end users setting in Admin Center without full admin access. It covers access, authentication, registration, allowlists, blocklists, account emails, profile and password editing, organization settings, and more. See Creating custom roles and assigning agents.
  • Automatic agent status changes let admins configure omnichannel routing to switch agents to a new unified status after a set number of consecutive missed voice or messaging assignments, helping reroute work faster. See Configuring missed assignment, idle timeout, and disconnection settings for unified agent statuses.
  • Custom role brand permissions now let admins delegate brand management to department managers and team leads without full admin access. The new Manage brands and Delete brands permissions can be scoped to all brands or only assigned brands. See Creating custom roles and assigning agents.

Knowledge

  • Front, KnowledgeOwl, Kustomer, Stoplight, Gong, Dynamics365, Linear, Shopify, Zammad, Airtable, Comm100, Halo, ServiceNow, Stonly, and Vimeo external knowledge sources are available. Connect them to power AI agents, admin copilot, help center search, and generative search. See Connecting external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account.
  • The CSV uploader lets Knowledge admins upload CSV files as external knowledge content when no connector or REST API is available. Uploaded rows become external content records that can power Zendesk AI and search. See Connecting external knowledge content using uploaded CSV files.
  • Bulk AI translations for articles lets Enterprise users generate help center article translations in bulk from the new editor, translate into multiple supported languages at once, and exclude specific terms. See Translating articles in your help center using AI.
  • Universal knowledge connector now supports OAuth 2.0 client credentials for compatible REST/JSON sources and AI-assisted field and pagination mapping, making it easier to connect external knowledge and sync content. See Connecting external content using the universal knowledge connector.

Contact Center

  • Summaries in call notifications now appear before agents accept incoming calls, giving them customer context via custom contact flow text or a Copilot-generated ticket summary. See Configuring summaries in Contact Center call notifications.
  • Contact Center After Call Work is now less disruptive and more flexible, letting agents finish wrap-up from the ticket call bar, keep workspace information visible, and start an outbound call before returning to the incoming-call queue. See Managing calls in Contact Center.

Workforce management

  • Forecast settings now has a dedicated page in Zendesk WFM, letting admins manage scenario settings separately from the forecast view. The new layout groups related forecasting options into clearer sections, making scenarios easier to configure and extend. See Setting up WFM forecasting.

Quality assurance

  • The quality assurance (QA) spotlights experience now includes system spotlight toggles and a cleaner conversation view with a separate Not matched drawer and on-demand Deep evaluation and verification. See Understanding spotlight insights.

Apps and integrations

  • Zendesk Support for Jira integration now supports Jira Data Center 11.3 LTS, allowing customers to keep creating and linking issues, syncing fields, and using the dedicated integration user option after upgrading. See Setting up the Zendesk Support for Jira integration.
  • QuickBooks Online and Xero connectors are now available in action flows, letting teams find and update accounting records from Zendesk workflows. This helps manage billing-related tasks more consistently and reduces switching between systems. See Action flow steps and actions reference.
  • OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude connectors now support the latest models, with dynamic model selection based on the connected account so newly supported models appear automatically. See Action flow steps and actions reference.
  • Action flows now support Trello and Jira Service Management connectors, letting admins build workflows that manage cards and requests, including comments, assignments, approvals, and lookups. See Action flow steps and actions reference.
  • Salesforce actions in action flows now support custom fields and standard or custom objects, letting admins map Salesforce data and automate workflows more flexibly across account, contact, lead, opportunity, case, and campaign records. See Action flow steps and actions reference.

articles.name: Authentication error: SMTP authentication not provided or not supported
articles.title: Authentication error: SMTP authentication not provided or not supported
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I am trying to integrate an email account to my sales account, previously named Sell. I followed the steps to add my email and see the error message: Authentication: SMTP authentication not provided or not supported. Please check your SMTP configuration settings.

Resolution steps

The error message Authentication: SMTP authentication not provided or not supported indicates that the authorization of your OAUTH application on the Office 365 side was successful. However, Zendesk ran into an SMTP AUTH error when connecting the integration.

To resolve your issue

  1. Ask your email admin to enable SMTP AUTH on your email account. For more information, see the article: Use the Microsoft 365 admin center to enable or disable SMTP AUTH on specific mailboxes
  2. After enabling the email protocol, integrate your Office 365 email
Note: Enabling SMTP alone will not resolve this error message. This email protocol is often turned off in Office 365 by default. Your email admin must turn on both IMAP and SMTP and SMTP AUTH for your mailbox, as sales uses these protocols to synchronize and send emails to your account.

For more information, see the article: Troubleshooting email integration errors.

articles.name: Workflow recipe: Recording a Contact Center IVR selection on a ticket
articles.title: Workflow recipe: Recording a Contact Center IVR selection on a ticket
articles.body:
You can use an Amazon Connect contact flow and Contact Center to record a caller's interactive voice response (IVR) menu selection on a ticket. This workflow uses a contact attribute, a dropdown ticket field, and the field options' tags.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

Record callers’ IVR menu selections on tickets by setting Amazon Connect contact attributes and mapping them to a dropdown ticket field. Matching attribute values to field option tags lets agents see whether a caller selected Billing, Sales, or Support. This workflow provides request context; it does not assign tickets to groups or change call routing.

You can use an Amazon Connect contact flow and Contact Center to record a caller's interactive voice response (IVR) menu selection on a ticket. This workflow uses a contact attribute, a dropdown ticket field, and the field options' tags.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Workflow goal
  • Adding the contact attribute to the IVR branches
  • Preparing a ticket field for the selection
  • Mapping the attribute to the ticket field
  • Testing the workflow

Workflow goal

You want agents to see which department a caller selected in the IVR menu, so they have context about the request when they open the ticket.

In this example, your menu offers Billing, Sales, and Support. After you configure the workflow, the following happens:

  1. A caller selects Billing, Sales, or Support in the IVR menu.
  2. The contact flow sets a contact attribute to the value for that selection.
  3. Contact Center maps the attribute to the Contact group ticket field.
  4. The ticket shows the selected option and its associated tag.

This workflow records the selection. It doesn't assign the ticket to a Zendesk group or change call routing.

Before you begin

For this example, you need:

  • Zendesk Contact Center connected to Amazon Connect
  • An Amazon Connect flow with an IVR menu and branches for Billing, Sales, and Support
  • Access to edit and publish the flow, create or edit ticket fields, and configure contact attribute mappings
  • An agent available to answer test calls

You can adapt the field name, attribute key, options, and tags to your own workflow. Use the same attribute key in the flow and mapping, and use each option's tag as the corresponding attribute value in the flow.

Adding the contact attribute to the IVR branches

Configure the flow to record the selection. Use the same key on all branches and a different value for each selection. The key and values in this recipe are examples. If you use an existing ticket field, use its option tags as the corresponding values.

To set the contact attribute

  1. In Amazon Connect, select Routing > Flows, then open the flow that contains the IVR menu.
  2. Add a Set contact attributes block to the Billing branch after the caller selects the option.
    • Configure the block to set a user-defined attribute on the current contact:
      • Key: contact_group
      • Value: contact_group_billing
    • Confirm the block's configuration and connect its success and error paths to the appropriate parts of your flow.
  3. Add a Set contact attributes block on the Sales branch, using the key contact_group and value contact_group_sales.

    Confirm and connect the second block's success and error paths.

  4. Add a Set contact attributes block on the Support branch, using the key contact_group and value contact_group_support.

    Confirm and connect the third block's success and error paths, then save and publish the flow.

For more information about the block, see Set contact attributes in the AWS documentation.

Preparing a ticket field for the selection

Next, create a dropdown ticket field or use an existing one. The option tags must match the values you set in the flow. Changing tags on an existing field can affect tickets; see Understanding how custom ticket field options and associated tags interact.

To prepare the ticket field

  1. In Admin Center, click Objects and rules in the sidebar, then select Tickets > Fields.
  2. Click Add field and select Drop-down, or open an existing dropdown field.
  3. For a new field, enter Contact group as the field name.
  4. Add or check the following options and their associated tags:
    • Billing: contact_group_billing
    • Sales: contact_group_sales
    • Support: contact_group_support

  5. Click Save.
  6. Select Tickets > Forms, to check that the field is on the ticket form used for your calls.

    If needed, add the field to the ticket form so agents can see it on tickets.

Mapping the attribute to the ticket field

Map the contact attribute to the field so the selection appears on the ticket.

To map the attribute

  1. In Contact Center, under General, click Contact attributes.
  2. Click Add new attribute.
  3. Enter contact_group as the contact attribute key and select Contact group as the ticket field.
  4. Click Add contact attribute.

The key must match the key used in all flow branches. For more information, see Adding call information using Amazon Connect attributes.

Testing the workflow

Test all three menu options to confirm that the field and tag match the caller's selection.

To test the workflow

  1. Refresh the Zendesk workspace.
  2. Place a test call, select Billing in the IVR menu, and have an agent answer.
  3. Open the call's ticket and check that the Contact group field is set to Billing and the contact_group_billing tag is present.
  4. Repeat the test with Sales and check that the field is set to Sales and the contact_group_sales tag is present.
  5. Repeat the test with Support and check that the field is set to Support and the contact_group_support tag is present.

If the field isn't visible on the ticket, check that it's included in the ticket form. If the expected value isn't set, check the flow branches, matching keys and tags, and mapping.

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I record a caller’s IVR selection on a Zendesk ticket?

Set a contact attribute in each Amazon Connect IVR branch after the caller makes a selection, using the same key (for example, `contact_group`) and the corresponding dropdown option tag as the value. In Contact Center, map that key to the dropdown ticket field. The ticket then shows the selected option and its associated tag.

How do I prepare the ticket field so it reflects the caller’s selection?

Create or use a dropdown ticket field and make sure its options have tags that match the values set in the flow. In this example, Billing uses `contact_group_billing`, Sales uses `contact_group_sales`, and Support uses `contact_group_support`. Ensure the field is included on the ticket form used for calls so agents can see it.

What do I need before I set up this workflow?

You need Zendesk Contact Center connected to Amazon Connect, an Amazon Connect flow with an IVR menu and branches for the options, access to edit and publish the flow and configure ticket fields and attribute mappings, and an agent available to answer test calls.

How do I test the workflow and troubleshoot a missing or incorrect selection?

Refresh the Zendesk workspace, place a test call for each menu option, and check the ticket’s field value and associated tag. If the field is not visible, check that it is included on the ticket form. If the expected value is missing, check the flow branches, matching attribute keys and tags, and the mapping.

Can I use this workflow to assign a ticket to a Zendesk group or change call routing?

No. This workflow records the caller’s IVR selection on the ticket; it does not assign the ticket to a Zendesk group or change call routing.

articles.name: Can I wipe or reset my Zendesk account to its default state?
articles.title: Can I wipe or reset my Zendesk account to its default state?
articles.body:
Question

Can I wipe or reset my Zendesk account to its default, original state?

Answer

No. There is no built-in "reset" or "wipe" button in Zendesk to restore an existing account or instance back to its original default state.

If you want a fresh start or clean slate, choose one of the options below depending on your needs:

Option 1: Cancel your current account and start a new one

If you want a completely fresh Zendesk instance with default configurations and no existing data:

  1. Ask your account owner to rename your current subdomain to something else, to free it up
  2. Cancel your current Zendesk subscription or account
  3. Sign up for a brand-new Zendesk account with the subdomain your previously owned
Warning: You cannot recover data from a canceled account after you close the account. Make sure to export any necessary ticket data, user profiles, or reports before canceling.

Option 2: Use a sandbox environment

If you want to test new workflows, configurations, or integrations without affecting your live production environment or needing a full account wipe:

  • Set up a sandbox environment, available on select Zendesk plans

Sandboxes allow you to test changes, build new triggers, or experiment safely without altering or deleting your production data.

Option 3: Manually delete unwanted data and configurations

If you want to keep your current account domain, subscription, or specific settings, you can manually remove unwanted items:

  • Tickets: Bulk delete tickets or use application programming interface (API) scripts for large-volume deletions
  • Users and organizations: Delete test users, end users, or inactive agents
  • Business rules: Manually delete or deactivate unwanted triggers, automations, macros, and views
  • Help center in Knowledge: Delete or unpublish test articles, categories, and sections
