  • Universal Connector:
    • Added OAuth 2.0 (client credentials) as an authentication option in the connector wizard, with credentials validated through ZIS and error states surfaced in the UI
    • Added AI-assisted field and pagination mapping — admins get editable, AI-prefilled mapping suggestions on create and when editing a connection without a mapping.

Help Center

  • Copenhagen request-list filters: Added an option in the updated Copenhagen theme to disable brand-based filtering of ticket fields; filtering stays on by default. Install the updated theme to use it.
Fixed

Article Editor

  • Excluded terms with ampersand: Fixed AI article translations ignoring excluded terms when the list contains an ampersand (or mixed phrase/word terms). Customer confirmed working. (OH-4970, PR #1318)
  • Content blocks in accordions/tabs: Restricted content blocks inside advanced components so the article editor stays aligned with the markup schema. (OH-4973, PR #18158)
  • Read-only recommendation articles: Opening a recommendation on API/legacy articles now skips read-only mode and shows the formatting warning banner (migration warning modal removed). (OH-4929, PR #18093)

AI agents

New

AI Agents Insights

  • Article and procedure recommendations for email: AI agent onboarding now includes article and procedure recommendations for the email channel.

Contact Center

Fixed

  • Contact Center
    • Voicemail tickets now keep tags added by triggers and business rules when the voicemail tag is applied.
    • Dialer country selection now includes more countries supported by Amazon Connect, including Iraq and Laos. If these countries don't appear, refresh your browser.

Quality assurance

New

  • Zendesk will update the AI model that powers AutoQA on November 11, 2026, as part of its ongoing effort to provide efficient, modern service. Because AI models can interpret prompt instructions differently, this update may affect category accuracy scores and overall AutoQA ratings. If your organization uses custom AutoQA prompts, you may need to adjust them to align with the new model.
  • AutoQA System Spotlights
    • You can now turn System Spotlights on or off and use an enhanced Spotlight experience.

App Marketplace

New

  • Watari (Support)
    • Watari turns selected Zendesk tickets—including screenshots, recordings, PDFs, voice notes, and logs—into structured bug reports with severity, reproduction steps, and customer impact. It ranks likely files and functions in a connected codebase and groups duplicate reports into one issue linked to the original tickets. It can prepare draft pull requests and customer updates for review. Updates are posted only after someone approves them and deployment is confirmed.
  • RoutIQ (Support)
    • RoutIQ scores available agents based on learned skill profiles, current workload, and recent assignments, then routes incoming tickets using view-based policies or direct-route rules. In the ticket sidebar, it can show agents the matched rule, selected agent, and runner-up. It also retries failed routing jobs. Optional AI classification can route tickets by topic, product area, or customer segment.
  • Ringly AI (Support)
    • Ringly AI’s phone agent answers calls to Shopify stores, looks up orders, tracks shipments, and handles common questions about products, shipping, and returns. It creates Zendesk tickets when callers ask to speak to someone, need support, or request a cancellation. Tickets can include a call summary, transcript, and call link. Ringly AI can also create a solved ticket with an internal note for every call it resolves.
  • Streamkap (Support)
    • Streamkap streams selected Zendesk data to destinations such as Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, ClickHouse, Redshift, and S3, with each resource organized as its own table. It can sync tickets and their comments, audits, metrics, and side conversations, along with users, organizations, groups, and support settings.
  • Syft by Veryation (Support) (paid)
    • Syft helps teams manage suspended tickets with rules that match senders, support addresses, subjects, message text, or suspension reasons. It can recover, delete, or hold a ticket for review, and supports delays so teams can review messages before rules run. Preview what rules will do, recover or delete tickets manually, and download run histories as CSV. Syft can run rules automatically every few minutes while an authorized agent or admin has Zendesk open.
  • Offshoot by Veryation (Support) (paid)
    • Offshoot separates an unrelated question from an existing ticket by creating a second, linked ticket, so each issue can have its own status and assignee. Agents can choose which messages to move, review a suggested subject, select the requester or a copied recipient, and carry over fields, CCs, tags, and attachments.
  • OTISA FollowUp (Support) (paid)
    • OTISA FollowUp lets agents schedule up to three future messages from a ticket. Any remaining messages are canceled automatically if the customer replies. FollowUp can draft a message based on the public conversation, the customer’s language, and the agent’s writing style. Agents can edit each draft and must schedule it themselves. An overview shows scheduled and sent messages, replies, pending follow-ups, and failures.
  • KaiCalls (Support)
    • KaiCalls provides a business phone line with an automated secretary that can take messages, answer common questions, book appointments, and send missed-call alerts. It can create a Zendesk ticket for each completed incoming call, with a private note containing the caller’s details, call summary, time, outcome, and a link to the call record. Set the group, priority, and tags for new tickets, and check call IDs to avoid duplicate tickets.
  • WitAsk by Witbor (Support)
    • WitAsk by Witbor lets support teams send forms to customers through WhatsApp from a ticket, or start a WhatsApp conversation with a form from Zendesk’s top bar. Forms can include text questions, choices, dropdowns, and dates. Teams can build them with a visual editor or get help from AI. WitAsk can map answers to Zendesk ticket or user fields, manage reusable message templates, and show sends, responses, and response rates.
  • PDF Export (Support) (paid)
    • PDF Export turns help center articles into print-ready PDFs that preserve headings, images, tables, and lists, and include source links, update dates, page numbers, and repeated table headers. It can also create ticket PDFs with key fields, the conversation, and attachment links. Agents can find articles or tickets by search, link, ID, or ticket number.
  • Zipchat (Support)
    • Zipchat is an AI support agent for online stores. It learns from a merchant’s website, products, and policies, then answers shoppers across chat, email, WhatsApp, and social channels. Zipchat replies to Zendesk tickets as an assigned agent and hands conversations to the team with an internal note when a customer asks for a person or needs human help.
  • Ticket Merge (Support) (paid)
    • Ticket Merge helps agents compare related tickets, choose which one to keep, and combine work from the ticket sidebar. Batch merging can include multiple source tickets. It displays saved details in a comparison view before confirmation, records merge operations so agents can check interrupted merges, and can restore a closed merged source as a new ticket with its private history.
  • Ticket Flagging (Support)
    • Ticket Flagging lets agents pin important past conversations from ticket, requester, or organization views and reopen them when they need context. Requester and organization lists stay separate, giving teams a shared reference for individual customer history and organization-wide context.
  • Macro Governance (Support)
    • Macro Governance gives admins usage counts and filters for unused, low-use, recently edited, inactive, and personal macros, with CSV export for review. It supports bulk edits with before-and-after previews and undo, version comparison and restore, and a duplicate finder for macros with similar titles or actions.
  • Super Duper Search (Support) (paid)
    • Super Duper Search helps admins search Zendesk configuration, Dynamic Content, and help center catalogs, then review results and coverage before exporting. It creates readable Excel workbooks that group macro and rule conditions with their actions, link records to their source IDs, and show comment text without HTML.
  • Rastro for Bling (Support) (paid)
    • Rastro for Bling matches a ticket requester to a Bling customer by email, CPF, or CNPJ, and shows the customer’s latest orders and their status in the ticket sidebar. It also shows invoice details with a DANFE link, copyable tracking codes, and pending boleto or Pix charges with payment links.
  • Scheduled Out of Office (Support) (paid)
    • Scheduled Out of Office lets agents schedule whole days or specific hours away from the app’s sidebar. Admins can schedule time for anyone and view the team’s bookings. The app changes an agent’s status when their leave begins and restores their previous status when it ends, using each agent’s time zone.
  • ResolveGuard (Support) (paid)
    • ResolveGuard checks tickets when agents try to mark them as solved. For matching damaged-item cases, it can require a resolution summary and image attachment. The ticket sidebar shows each requirement as passed or failed, and ResolveGuard blocks the save with a message if required evidence is missing.
  • Auditrak.ai (Support) (paid)
    • Auditrak.ai analyzes Zendesk conversations within a selected date range and scope, such as brand, form, group, channel, or tags, to investigate a business question. It highlights recurring requests and provides examples for review, helping teams find gaps in help content, forms, routing, procedures, or processes. Auditrak.ai provides findings in the app. An optional paid Advisor report includes an executive summary, demand breakdown, suggested next steps, limitations, and example tickets.
  • Ticket PDF & Attachments (Support)
    • Ticket PDF & Attachments adds a tool to the ticket sidebar for printing or saving a readable PDF with ticket participants, organization, group, brand, labeled custom fields, tags, and the full conversation.

articles.name: Connecting external content from any knowledge source using the universal knowledge connector
articles.title: Connecting external content from any knowledge source using the universal knowledge connector
articles.body:
You can use a universal knowledge connector (shown as theOthertile on the Connections page) to connect an external knowledge source to Zendesk when a dedicated knowledge connector isn't available for that source. The universal connector retrieves content through the source's REST API and makes that content available in Zendesk as external knowledge.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support with Knowledge Professional or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can use the universal knowledge connector to add content from an API-accessible wiki or knowledge base when no dedicated connector is available. Connect with an API key or OAuth 2.0, then review suggested or manually configure field mappings and pagination before syncing. The connector supports REST APIs that return JSON and refreshes content every 24 hours.

You can use a universal knowledge connector (shown as the Other tile on the Connections page) to connect an external knowledge source to Zendesk when a dedicated knowledge connector isn't available for that source. The universal connector retrieves content through the source's REST API and makes that content available in Zendesk as external knowledge.

When you configure a universal connector, you provide the information Zendesk needs to access the source API, including its API endpoint and credentials. You can authenticate with an API key or with OAuth 2.0 client credentials. Zendesk makes a request to the source to validate the connection and retrieve a sample response. Zendesk can then suggest field mappings and pagination settings based on that sample response. You review and edit those suggestions or map fields manually before you sync. If the source returns records across multiple pages, you configure how Zendesk retrieves subsequent pages.

This article contains the following topics:
  • API requirements
  • Connecting external content from any knowledge source with an API
  • Universal knowledge connector field mapping and pagination settings

API requirements

The universal connector is intended for API-accessible wikis and knowledge bases that meet the following API requirements:
  • Interface: REST API
  • Request method: GET
  • Response format: JSON
  • Authentication: API key or OAuth 2.0 client credentials
  • Record retrieval: Content and required metadata must be available in each retrieved record
  • Pagination: Configurable pagination
  • Synchronization: Full refresh every 24 hours

Connecting external content from any knowledge source with an API

You must be a Knowledge admin to configure the universal connector. You should also be familiar with the API for the knowledge source you're connecting.

To connect external content using the universal knowledge connector
  1. In Knowledge admin, click Content () in the sidebar.
  2. Click External content > Connections.
  3. Under the Available sources section, click Other.
  4. Review messaging about syncing knowledge with an API and click Continue to begin configuring the connection.
    Note: The universal connector uses the permissions associated with the API credentials used to configure the connection. Source-specific permissions for individual users or records aren't preserved or enforced in Zendesk.
  5. Enter the required authentication information to give Zendesk permission to access content from the knowledge source.

    Zendesk will send a request to the configured endpoint to verify that it can reach the source and authenticate using the credentials you provided.

    • Name: Identifier that you want to assign to the connection.
    • API URL: API endpoint for the source content.
    • Query parameters: Optional key-value pair appended to the end of the API URL to control the data returned in the endpoint response. You can enter up to five query parameters. To configure a query parameter, select the Query Parameters check box, then enter the Parameter and Value in the fields provided.
    • API key: API key to identify and authenticate Zendesk when making requests to the API. This key is usually generated in your developer or API settings.
    • OAuth 2.0 client credentials: Client ID, Client secret, and Token URL required for machine-to-machine access. Scopes are optional. No provider login redirect is required.
  6. After Zendesk validates the connection, review the field mappings and pagination settings. Values may be prefilled as AI suggestions based on the sample response.

    Edit any suggested values as needed or complete the mappings manually if suggestions are incomplete or unavailable.

  7. Click Sync.

    The knowledge connector is added to the Connections page and begins syncing. To manage existing connections, see Managing external knowledge connections.

Universal knowledge connector field mapping and pagination settings

Field mappings determine how content and metadata returned by the source API are stored as external content in Zendesk. After a successful connection test, field mappings and pagination may be prefilled as AI suggestions based on the sample response. Review and edit those suggestions before syncing.

Field mapping reference

  • Unique identifier: Required identifier for each item
  • Title: Article heading
  • Body: Content AI features use
  • URL: Public content URL
  • Last updated: When the content last changed
  • Locale: Content language

Pagination reference

  • Cursor: Uses a unique identifier or token to mark the position in the dataset. When selected, configure the following values:
    • Cursor parameter (required): The query parameter name your API expects on the next request (for example, cursor, after, or pageToken). Zendesk sends this parameter with the cursor value from the previous response. The first request is sent without this parameter.
    • Cursor location in response (required): The dot-notation path to the next cursor value in the JSON response (for example, meta.next_cursor or pagination.next).
    • Last page detection (optional): The dot-notation path to a boolean field that indicates whether more pages exist (for example, meta.has_more). Leave this blank if your API signals the last page by returning a null or empty cursor.
  • Offset: Specifies the starting point in the dataset and the maximum number of records to include on each page. When selected, configure the following values:
    • Page parameter: Parameter that Zendesk sends to request the next page (usually page, offset, or skip.
    • First page value: Value expected by the API. Selecting the wrong value skips the first batch.
  • Next link: API server provides the complete, pre-formatted URL for the next page directly inside its response. When selected, configure the following values:
    • Next link location in response: Where the next page URL sits in the response (usually next, next-page, or inside a links object.
  • Next link header: Zendesk looks for the next keyword in response headers.
  • None: Zendesk fetches all content in one request.

Article Q&A

Click to view

Can I connect a knowledge source that doesn't have a dedicated Zendesk connector?

Yes. Use the universal connector, shown as the Other tile on the Connections page. The source must provide a REST API that uses GET requests, returns JSON, supports API key or OAuth 2.0 client-credentials authentication, includes content and required metadata in each record, and supports configurable pagination. Zendesk performs a full refresh every 24 hours.

How do I configure the universal knowledge connector, and what access permissions does it use?

You must be a Knowledge admin and should be familiar with the source API. In Knowledge admin, go to Content > External content > Connections, choose Other, and continue. Enter a connection name, API URL, and credentials; you can also add up to five optional query parameters. Use an API key or provide the OAuth 2.0 client ID, client secret, and token URL (scopes are optional). Zendesk tests the connection, then you review the mappings and pagination settings and click Sync. The connector uses the permissions of the configured API credentials; individual user or record permissions from the source aren't preserved or enforced in Zendesk.

What content fields do I need to map before syncing my external knowledge?

Map the required unique identifier for each item and the applicable fields: Title (article heading), Body (content used by AI features), URL (public content URL), Last updated (when content last changed), and Locale (content language). Zendesk may suggest mappings from a sample response, but review and edit them or complete them manually before syncing.

What pagination options can I use when my knowledge source returns multiple pages?

Choose the method supported by your API: Cursor uses a token or identifier from the previous response; configure the query parameter and the cursor's location in the JSON response, with optional last-page detection. Offset uses a page parameter and first-page value. Next link uses a complete next-page URL in the response, while Next link header looks for the word `next` in response headers. Choose None if Zendesk should fetch all content in one request.

Why might the first batch of my content be skipped with offset pagination?

The offset pagination setting may have the wrong First page value. Set it to the value expected by your API; selecting the wrong value skips the first batch.

articles.name: Connecting external knowledge content using CSV files
articles.title: Connecting external knowledge content using CSV files
articles.body:
If your knowledge is stored in a spreadsheet or other system that can export a CSV (comma-separated values) file, you can upload it to Zendesk as external content. Use this option when no dedicated knowledge connector or REST API is available.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support with Knowledge Professional or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Upload CSV files to make spreadsheet or system content available as external knowledge for search, AI agents, Copilot, and workflows when no connector or REST API is available. Each row becomes a content record, not a help center article. You can group files under source names, but uploads don’t sync with the original file; to update or remove records, replace the connection.

If your knowledge is stored in a spreadsheet or other system that can export a CSV (comma-separated values) file, you can upload it to Zendesk as external content. Use this option when no dedicated knowledge connector or REST API is available.

Each content row in your file becomes one external content record, available wherever external content is used in Zendesk. The upload does not create help center articles.

You must be a Knowledge admin to upload files and manage the connection. No authentication to the source system is required.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Preparing the CSV file
  • Choose a source name for each CSV file
  • Uploading the CSV file
  • Updating or removing uploaded content

Preparing the CSV file

Before uploading, check that your file uses the supported columns and format and fits within your account’s limits.

Check your CSV file headers

The first row of the CSV file must contain column headers. Include the required headers, title and body, and any optional headers you need: locale, url, and labels.

Header names are not case-sensitive. Each header can appear only once. Files with duplicate or unsupported headers are not imported.
Table 1. Supported CSV columns
Column Required Description
title Yes The record’s heading. Cannot be empty. Titles longer than 255 characters are shortened to 255 characters.
body Yes The record’s content, used by search and AI features. Cannot be empty. Supports plain text or Markdown, which Zendesk converts to HTML. Content larger than 500 KB (500,000 bytes) is shortened to that size.
locale No The content’s language, such as en-us. Use a locale enabled in your Help Center so the record can appear in search. Leave blank to let Zendesk detect the language from the body.
url No An HTTP or HTTPS address for the content in your source system. Leave blank if the record has no URL.
labels No Comma-separated labels in a single cell. Spaces around each label are trimmed. Leave blank if the record has no labels.

Format the CSV file content

Add one content record per row. You can use a comma (,) or semicolon (;) to separate values in the CSV file. If a value contains a comma or a line break, enclose it in double quotes.

For labels, enter all labels in one cell, separated by commas. Enclose the cell in double quotes when it contains more than one label. For example:

title,body,labels
Example,Article text,"billing, how to"

This creates a record with two labels: billing and how to.

Each label must contain text. A cell such as "billing,,how to" is invalid because it contains an empty label. If the record has no labels, leave the cell blank.

Save the file and review the limits

Save the file as comma-separated values with a .csv extension. Both .csv and .CSV are accepted.

The filename must end in .csv. Files named notes.csv.txt or report.csv.exe are not accepted. Other formats are not supported. Empty, zero-byte files are also rejected.

The following limits apply:

Limit Value
Files per upload 10
File size 20 MB per file
Files stored per account 200
Record count Rows count toward the account external content record limit: 50,000 records, or 100,000 records on Enterprise.

Each imported content row counts toward your account’s external content record limit. This limit is shared across all external content sources in the account.

Storage limits also depend on your plan. See Managing data storage in your Zendesk account.

Choose a source name for each CSV file

When you set up a CSV connection, assign a source name to each file you upload. The Connections page shows both the file name and source name. When you connect CSV content to an AI agent, Copilot, or another application, you’ll select the source name. The file name isn’t listed as a knowledge source there.

Choose a source name that helps admins identify the content they want to connect. You can use one source name for multiple CSV files to group them, or use a separate source name for each file. If you use a separate name for each file, consider using the file name as the source name.

Uploading the CSV file

When your files are ready, you can upload them from the Connections page.

Zendesk stores and reads the uploaded file once. Changes to your original spreadsheet are not synced automatically.

If the import fails, the connection shows a failed state. Errors can affect an entire file or an individual row:

  • File errors: If Zendesk cannot parse a file, none of its records are imported, including rows before the error. Files with invalid headers are also rejected.
  • Row errors: If a row has an empty title or body, an invalid URL or locale, or invalid labels, that row is skipped. Other valid rows in the file are imported.

To upload a CSV file

  1. In Knowledge admin, click Content () in the sidebar.
  2. Click External content > Connections.
  3. Under Upload files, click Select files.

  4. Review the messaging, then click Next.

  5. On the Upload files page, click Choose file, or drag your CSV files onto the page. You can add up to ten files.

  6. Click Next.

  7. Select or enter a source name for each file, then click Next.

    The source name is required and can contain up to 32 characters. New source names must be unique within your account. You can select an existing source name for multiple files. Knowledge source names are used to identify knowledge sources when using external content in workflows.

Zendesk adds the connection to the Connections page and starts importing in the background. A file is marked as completed only after its records have been created.

Updating or removing uploaded content

The connection contains the records created from your uploaded files. Because Zendesk does not monitor the original files, editing your spreadsheet does not update those records.

Uploading an updated file creates new records. It does not replace records from an earlier upload.

To replace the content from a connection:

  1. Update your original file and save the corrected version as a CSV file.
  2. Delete the existing connection. This removes all external content records created from that source.
  3. Upload the corrected file as a new source.

You cannot use the uploader to delete an individual record from an imported file. To remove a row, remove it from your CSV file, then replace the connection using the steps above.

For more information about managing or deleting connections, see Managing external knowledge connections.

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I format a CSV file before uploading it as external content?

Use a first row of headers with the required `title` and `body` columns. Optional columns are `locale`, `url`, and `labels`. Add one record per row; use commas or semicolons to separate values, and enclose values containing commas or line breaks in double quotes. Put multiple comma-separated labels in one quoted cell, and don’t include empty labels. Save the file with a `.csv` extension. Each row becomes an external content record; the upload does not create Help Center articles.

What file and record limits apply when I upload CSV content?

You can upload up to 10 files at a time, each up to 20 MB, and store up to 200 files per account. The external content record limit is 50,000 records, or 100,000 on Enterprise, shared across all external content sources. Required titles and bodies cannot be empty; titles over 255 characters and bodies over 500 KB are shortened. Empty files and files with unsupported or duplicate headers are rejected.

How do I upload CSV files and choose a source name?

You must be a Knowledge admin. In Knowledge admin, go to Content > External content > Connections, click Select files under Upload files, review the messaging, and choose or drag in up to 10 CSV files. Continue through the steps and select or enter a required source name for each file. A new name must be unique in your account and can contain up to 32 characters; you can reuse an existing name for multiple files. When connecting content to an AI agent, Copilot, or another application, you select the source name, not the file name.

Why did my CSV import fail or skip some records?

If Zendesk cannot parse a file or its headers are invalid, none of that file’s records are imported. If an individual row has an empty title or body, an invalid URL or locale, or invalid labels, that row is skipped while other valid rows are imported. The connection shows a failed state if the import fails.

How can I update or remove content after uploading a CSV file?

Zendesk reads the uploaded file once, so edits to the original spreadsheet are not synced. Uploading an updated file creates new records rather than replacing the old ones. To replace content or remove a row, update the CSV, delete the existing connection (which removes all its records), and upload the corrected file as a new source. You cannot delete an individual imported record through the uploader.

articles.name: Service Incident - October 18, 2026 - AI Agents | Multiple Pods - Agent and customer messages not showing in AI Agents conversations
articles.title: Service Incident - October 18, 2026 - AI Agents | Multiple Pods - Agent and customer messages not showing in AI Agents conversations
articles.body:
Summary

Between 18:00 UTC on 16 October 2026 and 08:56 UTC on 21 October 2026, AI Agents Advanced customers hosted in the EU region experienced an issue affecting conversation history and analytics data across multiple pods.

During this period, agent and customer messages could be delayed or missing from conversation views, causing some conversation histories to appear incomplete. AI Agents Advanced analytics data associated with these conversations could also be delayed or unavailable.

Timeline

October 19, 2026 08:28 UTC | October 19, 2026 01:29 AM PT

We are aware that customers with AI Agents Advanced data hosted in the EU region may see missing or delayed agent and customer messages in conversation views, as well as missing or delayed analytics data. We understand that incomplete conversation history and reporting can disrupt your work, and we apologize for the impact. Our engineers have applied changes to restore processing and are monitoring recovery while the remaining backlog clears. Based on the current processing rate, we estimate the backlog will clear over the next few hours, with delayed data populating as it is processed. This estimate may change, and some remaining data gaps may require additional recovery work. We continue to investigate these gaps and will provide further updates as recovery progresses. Thank you for your patience while we work to restore complete visibility into your data.

October 19, 2026 10:59 UTC | October 19, 2026 03:59 AM PT

Our engineering teams have completed processing the majority of the backlog that caused agent and customer messages to be delayed or missing from conversation views. The remaining messages are still being processed, and work is also ongoing to restore the related analytics data. We are actively monitoring service performance and recovery progress to ensure that the remaining backlog is processed successfully. Please verify whether the messages that were previously missing are now visible in your conversation views. If any messages remain unavailable or delayed, please contact us with the affected conversation details and approximate message times so that we can investigate further.

October 19, 2026 17:13 UTC | October 19, 2026 10:13 AM PT

Our continued work to backfill missed agent and customer messages in conversation views has uncovered another subset of messages to process. We are monitoring the backfill procedure and our initial estimates show it will be completed tomorrow, Tuesday October 20th. We will provide an update when we can narrow the timeline or if we need to amend the completion target date.

October 20, 2026 08:49 UTC | October 20, 2026 01:49 AM PT

Most previously delayed conversation messages have been processed, but some historical messages remain missing and recovery is not yet complete. We paused the historical message recovery process after it caused delays in another part of the service. Those additional delays have now cleared, and our engineers are developing a revised approach to resume recovery while protecting service stability. We currently do not have a revised completion time; however, we will share further updates once the revised recovery plan and timeline are confirmed. We apologize for the continued disruption.

October 20, 2026 18:28 UTC | October 20, 2026 11:28 AM PT

We have another update on the recovery of missing or delayed AI Agent conversation messages. We are monitoring the backlog recovery process and anticipate the new completion date to be October 21st, 2026. Thank you for your understanding and patience. We'll be certain to update when the backlog processing is complete or any new information here.

October 21, 2026 08:22 UTC | October 21, 2026 01:22 AM PT

We have completed recovery of the historical agent and customer messages affected by this incident for AI Agents Advanced customers hosted in the EU region. Previously missing messages should now be visible in conversation views. We apologize for the disruption and thank you for your patience throughout the recovery.

 

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by an internal service capacity issue in the EU region following infrastructure interruptions. This delayed the processing of messages and reporting information, which caused some conversation history and analytics data to appear late or be temporarily unavailable.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we increased the capacity of the affected service and made stability improvements to prevent the problem from recurring during recovery. We then processed the delayed information and restored missing messages in affected conversation histories.

Remediation Items

  1. Implement on-call alerts for delayed message processing, service interruptions, and failures that prevent scheduled work from running.
  2. Create a documented response procedure for safely managing processing limits and recovering delayed messages.
  3. Strengthen capacity planning and release safeguards for the EU message-processing service.
  4. Implement a controlled process for restoring historical messages when delayed or missing information is identified.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Announcing the Knowledge Management API (EAP)
articles.title: Announcing the Knowledge Management API (EAP)
articles.body:
We’re inviting customers to try the Knowledge Management API through an Early Access Program (EAP). The API gives developers programmatic access to Knowledge articles, translations, reusable content blocks, and editorial workflows. Test it with your integrations and tell us what works well and what needs improvement.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

The Knowledge Management API brings article content and the workflows used to manage it into a REST API. The EAP covers the following capabilities:

  • Manage articles: Create, retrieve, archive, restore, and delete articles. Set article ownership, edit permissions, and verification status.
  • Manage translations: Create and update titles and content for individual languages, and set an article’s default language.
  • Manage editorial workflows: Assign translations to users, submit them for review, approve them, and publish or unpublish them. Schedule publication and unpublication for individual translations.
  • Manage reusable content blocks: List, create, retrieve, update, and delete content blocks through the API.
  • Place articles in your help center: Create placements that connect Knowledge articles to help center sections.

Creating an article and making it available in your help center are separate steps. A new article needs a placement to appear in Knowledge admin, and its translation must be published before readers can access it in the help center, subject to its visibility settings.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Customers use scripts, integrations, and external tools to manage their knowledge at scale. These workflows need access to article content and to the ownership, review, and publishing controls that support day-to-day content maintenance.

The Knowledge Management API is designed around the Knowledge editor’s content structure, including reusable content blocks. This gives developers a way to build content workflows that work with the editor. During the EAP, we want to understand how the API fits your publishing and localization processes and where you need additional capabilities.

What do I need to do?

You can start using the API immediately. No sign-up, approval, or additional activation is required to join the EAP. Use an authenticated agent or admin account with the permissions required for each operation.

Start with the API references provided as Markdown files:

  • Articles: knowledge_articles.md 
  • Translations: knowledge_article_translations.md 
  • Content blocks: knowledge_blocks.md 

For the supported content structure, see Supported HTML for help center articles.

Try the workflows that matter to your team, such as updating content through an integration, managing translations, or scheduling publication. Check the results in the Knowledge editor and your help center, and share any gaps or unexpected behavior.

Share your questions and feedback in our EAP Community: Knowledge Management API EAP welcome post. The welcome post explains how to report an issue or suggest an improvement. For general product assistance, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Getting started with agentic analytics
articles.title: Getting started with agentic analytics
articles.body:
Agentic analytics is Zendesk’s next-generation, AI-driven analytics experience. It lets you ask business questions in plain language, get cited, narrative answers, and build reports or dashboards without technical or Business Intelligence (BI) expertise. You'll do most of your work in analyst copilot, an AI-powered analytics assistant that investigates trends, builds dashboards, explains root causes, and remembers your analysis so future work is smarter and faster.

What's my plan?
All Suites Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support with Explore Professional or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Use agentic analytics to ask business questions in plain language and get answers with cited sources. Analyst copilot helps you investigate trends, create and customize reports, and build shareable dashboards without BI expertise. Organize work with projects and datasets, and save business logic as memories so future analyses are more consistent.

Important: Agentic analytics is free to use until January 31, 2027. After that date, usage for some features, including analyst copilot, real-time insights, and dataset builder will be charged. You’ll be notified before charges begin.

Agentic analytics is Zendesk’s next-generation, AI-driven analytics experience. It lets you ask business questions in plain language, get cited, narrative answers, and build reports or dashboards without technical or Business Intelligence (BI) expertise. You'll do most of your work in analyst copilot, an AI-powered analytics assistant that investigates trends, builds dashboards, explains root causes, and remembers your analysis so future work is smarter and faster.

In this guide, you'll learn about the basics of agentic analytics and how to get up and running quickly.

This article contains the following topics:

  • What is agentic analytics?
  • Accessing analyst copilot
  • Creating reports (the easier way)
  • Take control with report builder
  • Building dashboards
  • Organizing your work with projects, datasets, and memories
  • Sharing your work
  • Best practices
  • Agentic analytics for Explore users
  • Summary and next steps

Related articles

  • Resources for agentic analytics

What is agentic analytics?

With agentic analytics, you move from the manual world of traditional BI (think building dashboards, writing queries, wrangling data) to an interactive, ask-first system. Type your business question, and analyst copilot answers in context, cites its sources, and explains its reasoning. Each analysis is “remembered” as a memory, so future questions get smarter and analysis gets more consistent over time.

The key features of agentic analytics are:
  • Prebuilt analytical apps: Bundles the datasets, dashboards, and reports needed for common use cases, such as support, or AI agents. Using these "off-the-shelf" reports and dashboards can save you time and effort.
  • AI-assisted builders: Analyst copilot includes tools to help you create datasets, reports, and dashboards.
  • Analyst copilot: Create reports, dashboards, and investigate your data using a range of ai-assisted tools. Analyst copilot is where you'll do most of your work.
  • Context graph: A system of compounding intelligence that remembers every analysis, meaning better results over time.

Accessing analyst copilot

You'll find the analyst copilot icon in the Analytics section of your Zendesk account.

To access analyst copilot

  • In Analytics, click the Home () icon in the sidebar.

    The Home page appears, showing your projects, reports, dashboards, and a search box for natural language prompts.

  • Tip: If you don’t see the icon, contact your admin; you might need higher permissions.
The Home page includes the following elements:
  1. Question box: Enter natural language prompts to create reports, or search for existing assets to work with. See Creating analyst copilot reports using a prompt and Using natural language prompts to create reports in analyst copilot.
  2. Analysis mode: Choose the prompt type you want from the following:
    • Analyze data: Uses existing memories to create the report. This prompt type is suitable for most users.

  3. Suggested questions: Intelligently suggests reports you might want to generate based on your datasets.
  4. Recent items: Displays reports and dashboards you've recently accessed.
  5. Trending items: Displays the most popular reports and dashboards for all users.

Creating reports (the easier way)

You can generate reports by entering a prompt. You don't need to manually create reports..

Creating a quick report using a prompt

  1. On the analyst copilot home page, enter a prompt like “Show me tickets by channel this month.”

    Copilot builds a report, summarizes the findings, and cites the sources and memories that were used.

  2. Review and adjust measures, dimensions, filters, and visualizations as you like.

Take control with report builder

Sometimes, you'll need to generate complex reports that might need some manual work from you before they are ready. For example, a report might contain a particularly complex formula or you need to troubleshoot results that are not what you expected.

In these situations, use report builder; a set of tools you can use to customize virtually all aspects of your report.

Report builder includes the following elements:
  1. Dataset panel: Contains the various dataset elements you can choose from to create your reports. See Working with analyst copilot datasets.
  2. Visualization settings: Lets you choose from a range of different styles to present your report such as bar, donut, and line charts. See Understanding report visualizations in analyst copilot .
  3. Query controls: This is where you add dimensions, measures, date fields, and filters you can use to return the results you need. See Creating analyst copilot reports using report builder.
  4. Report preview: Shows a preview of how your finished report will look.
  5. Memories: Opens the context graph where you can interact with the memories that were used or created for this report. See Working with analyst copilot memories.
  6. Save report: Saves the most current version of your report.

You can use report builder to create a new report, edit an existing report created from a prompt, or edit a report you created in a previous report builder session.

For more help, see Creating reports in analyst copilot.

Building dashboards

Dashboards are collections of reports, filters, and insights that you can assemble for various audiences. You create and share dashboards from the dashboard builder tool located in analyst copilot.

Tip: Before you start creating dashboards, make sure to check whether the report you need is already contained in a prebuilt dashboard.
Dashboard builder includes the following elements:
  1. Component toolbar: Contains the building blocks you can use to build a dashboard such as reports, links, and text.
  2. Dashboard tabs: Create tabs to split your report into separate pages. See Creating and managing analyst copilot dashboards.
  3. Dashboard canvas: This is the area you'll drag and drop components into to build your dashboard.
  4. Save dashboard: Saves the current dashboard state.
  5. Edit and view: Dashboards feature two modes, view, and edit. To make changes to a dashboard, it must be in edit mode. See Creating and managing analyst copilot dashboards.

For more help, see Creating and managing analyst copilot dashboards.

Organizing your work with projects, datasets, and memories

Agentic analytics includes several features to help you manage your reports and business information:

  • Projects: Organize datasets, reports, dashboards, and memories in one place. Set permissions at the project or group level for secure collaboration. See Creating and managing analyst copilot projects
  • Datasets: Source data collections (e.g., tickets, agents, IT assets). While the included datasets cover most situations, you can build custom datasets using dataset builder for more complex needs. See Working with analyst copilot datasets
  • Memories: Analyst copilot saves every logical step, business rule, or key term you use. This makes future reports faster and more reliable because everyone uses the same definitions and logic. You can combine, narrate, rate, and fork memories for new reports or deeper insights. See Working with analyst copilot memories.

Sharing your work

When you've finished working on a dashboard, you'll likely want to share it with other people. Analyst copilot lets you share your dashboard In two formats:
  • Image: to download your dashboard as a JPEG image. You'll find the image in your Downloads folder.
  • URL: Copies a link to the dashboard to your computers clipboard. You can then share this URL with others on your team.

See Sharing dashboards.

Best practices

We've collected a large number of best practices to help you get the most from analyst copilot.

See Best practices for analyst copilot.

Agentic analytics for Explore users

If you're familiar with Explore, we've put together a guide that helps you understand the fundamental differences between Explore and agentic analytics. This will help you to get up and running as quickly as possible.

See Getting started with agentic analytics for Explore users.

Summary and next steps

Agentic analytics provides tools to go from questions to insights with no technical skills required. Just launch analyst copilot, and start asking your business questions. As you build, save key logic as memories, and use dashboards to share results. Over time, your analytics system gets smarter and more consistent, setting your team up for rapid, reliable insights.

We've created extensive documentation to help you get started and dig deeper into agentic analytics. See Resources for agentic analytics to get started.

Article Q&A

Click to view

How do I open analyst copilot, and what should I do if I can’t see it?

In Zendesk, open Analytics and click the Home icon in the sidebar. If the analyst copilot icon isn’t visible, contact your admin because you might need higher permissions.

How can I create a report by asking a question in plain language?

On the analyst copilot Home page, enter a prompt, such as “Show me tickets by channel this month.” Copilot creates a report, summarizes the findings, and cites the sources and memories it used. You can then adjust the report’s measures, dimensions, filters, and visualizations.

When should I use report builder, and what can I change there?

Use report builder for complex reports, such as ones involving a complex formula, or when you need to troubleshoot unexpected results. You can choose dataset elements and visualizations, add dimensions, measures, date fields, and filters, preview the report, interact with its memories, and save it. You can create a report or edit an existing one.

How can I organize analytics work and make future reports more consistent?

Use projects to organize datasets, reports, dashboards, and memories, with permissions set at the project or group level. Datasets provide source data, and you can build custom datasets for more complex needs. Analyst copilot saves logical steps, business rules, and key terms as memories; these help future reports use consistent definitions and logic.

How do I build and share a dashboard with my team?

Use dashboard builder in analyst copilot to assemble reports, filters, and insights. Add components to the canvas, use tabs to split content into pages, and save the dashboard. Switch to edit mode to make changes. You can share it by downloading a JPEG image or copying its URL to share with teammates.

articles.name: Understanding Zendesk Bridge and allowing external AI agents to perform actions in Zendesk (EAP)
articles.title: Understanding Zendesk Bridge and allowing external AI agents to perform actions in Zendesk (EAP)
articles.body:
Zendesk Bridge provides a way to establish governed connections between Zendesk and external AI agents your organization uses, including Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, or AI agents you build yourself. After you connect an external AI agent to Zendesk and assign tools to it, the agent can perform Zendesk actions, such as creating and updating tickets, looking up users and organizations, searching your help center, applying macros, and more.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Use Bridge to connect external AI agents to your support account and let them perform approved actions, such as creating tickets, finding users, and searching your help center. You control which agents connect and which tools they can use; access follows each user's permissions and actions are logged. During the early access program, destructive actions, bulk exports, and changes to admin settings aren't available.

Zendesk Bridge and external AI agents are currently in an early access program (EAP). During the EAP, Zendesk Bridge is available without charge. However, plan packaging and pricing might change when the feature becomes generally available. To participate, join the External AI EAP.

Zendesk Bridge provides a way to establish governed connections between Zendesk and external AI agents your organization uses, including Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, or AI agents you build yourself. After you connect an external AI agent to Zendesk and assign tools to it, the agent can perform Zendesk actions, such as creating and updating tickets, looking up users and organizations, searching your help center, applying macros, and more.

For example, you might ask an external AI agent to pull all open tickets for a customer, find similar issues that were resolved, and show a trend. Or you might ask an external agent to look at your ticket fields, macros, and triggers, and suggest a new escalation process or identify configurations that could be changed or added to streamline the existing escalation process.

A governed connection is an approved, controlled link between your Zendesk instance and an external AI agent. It lets the external agent use Zendesk capabilities while Zendesk administrators control which external agents can connect and which tools they can use.

This article describes what Zendesk Bridge and external AI agents are and essential information about using these features.

This article contains the following topics:
  • Considerations and essential facts about Zendesk Bridge and external agents
  • Understanding rate limits and usage allowances
  • Joining the External AI EAP
  • Getting help

Related article:

  • Zendesk Bridge FAQ

Considerations and essential facts about Zendesk Bridge and external agents

Before you start using Zendesk Bridge to connect to external agents, consider the following:
  • Zendesk Bridge separates connection, tool exposure, and authorization for external AI agents. Zendesk Bridge is the means by which external AI agents are connected to Zendesk and granted access to read and interact with data in your Zendesk account. The external agent's configuration controls which tools are available to that connection.
  • By default, external AI agents have no access. An external agent can use only the Zendesk tools you explicitly grant it access to.
  • A user who doesn't have permission to perform an action in Zendesk can't use an external AI agent to perform that action on their behalf. The request would be blocked because the external AI agents enforce the acting user's role, group access, and permissions at the time a tool or action is called.
  • The catalog of tools that can be assigned to external agents through Zendesk Bridge is extensive, including actions related to tickets, messaging, users, organizations, knowledge, Admin Center, and action flows. However, during the EAP, the following limitations apply to the available tools and actions:
    • Destructive actions, bulk exports, and third-party integrations aren't supported.
    • Admin Center actions are read-only. External agents can open Admin Center for context, search admin settings, and view usage summaries, but they can't create, modify, or delete settings.
  • External AI agents sign in to Zendesk with their own identity using standard OAuth 2.1. They never use human user credentials, such as email and password or API tokens.
  • Any external AI agent that uses standard OAuth grant types can connect to Zendesk Bridge, so you're not limited to specific protocols or integration models.
  • Some common external AI agents have been predefined to help you get started with external AI agents.
  • External AI agents can act on behalf of users, with the user's consent, or for anonymous users without their consent. Users can see which external AI agents have access to their data and can revoke that access at any time.
  • Transaction logs include records of which external AI agent performed each action and on whose behalf that action was taken.
  • Zendesk Bridge allows external AI agents to delegate tasks to approved Zendesk AI agents, which complete the task and return status and outcome to the original agent. However, the only Zendesk AI agent available during the EAP is a new Monitoring agent. See Using the Monitoring agent by Zendesk with external AI agents. Additional Zendesk agents may be added during or after EAP.
  • You can update, restrict, or disable an external AI agent's access at any time.

See also the Zendesk Bridge FAQ.

Understanding rate limits and usage allowances

Every capability an external AI agent uses through Zendesk Bridge is governed and metered as a unit of usage in the following ways:
  • Metering: Every interaction emits a billing-grade event capturing the agent, channel, skill, and outcome. Audit logs, operational reporting, and billing are based on the same source of truth. Billing-grade metering will be phased in through general availability in 2027.
  • Regulation: Your Zendesk subscription plan defines which Zendesk tools and actions are available to your external AI agents. Within the categories of tools and actions you have access to, you have granular control over which agents can discover, read, and perform specific tasks within your account.
  • Rate limiting: Layered limits at the tenant and agent level protect platform stability from infinite loops and abuse. In the future, they will also mark the boundary between included plan usage and paid consumption.

Joining the External AI EAP

External AI agents and Zendesk Bridge are available as part of an early access program. To participate, you must join the External AI EAP and agree to the terms and conditions.

To join the External AI EAP
  1. In Admin Center, click AI in the sidebar, then select External AI.
  2. Select External AI early access.
  3. Review the terms and conditions and click I agree.
  4. Click Submit.

Getting help

The help documentation for Zendesk Bridge and external AI agents consists of the following articles:

  • Understanding Zendesk Bridge and allowing external AI agents to perform actions in Zendesk
  • Zendesk Bridge FAQ
  • Connecting external AI agents to Zendesk
  • Monitoring external AI agents in Zendesk
  • Editing and managing external AI agents in Zendesk
  • Using the Monitoring agent by Zendesk with external AI agents
  • Using Zendesk playbooks with external AI agents
  • Using partner AI plugins with Zendesk

Article Q&A

Click to view

How can I use Zendesk Bridge with an external AI agent?

Zendesk Bridge creates a governed connection between Zendesk and an external AI agent. After you connect the agent and grant it specific tools, it can perform actions such as creating or updating tickets, looking up users and organizations, searching your help center, and applying macros.

How do I control what an external AI agent can access and do in Zendesk?

External AI agents have no access by default; administrators explicitly grant tools and can update, restrict, or disable access at any time. The agent uses its own identity through OAuth 2.1, and it cannot perform actions the acting user lacks permission to perform. Transaction logs record which agent acted and on whose behalf.

What actions are unavailable to my external AI agent during the EAP?

Destructive actions, bulk exports, and third-party integrations aren't supported. Admin Center actions are read-only: agents can view context, search settings, and view usage summaries, but can't create, modify, or delete settings.

How are my external AI agents' Zendesk usage and rate limits managed?

Each interaction produces a billing-grade event that records the agent, channel, skill, and outcome; audit logs, operational reporting, and billing use the same source. Your subscription plan defines available tools and actions, and layered tenant- and agent-level rate limits protect platform stability.

How do I join the External AI EAP, and is Zendesk Bridge free during it?

In Admin Center, select AI in the sidebar, then External AI, and choose External AI early access. Review and accept the terms, then click Submit. Zendesk Bridge is available without charge during the EAP, but plan packaging and pricing might change when it becomes generally available.

articles.name: Why does my SSL certificate still show "Replacement pending" after a successful upload?
articles.title: Why does my SSL certificate still show "Replacement pending" after a successful upload?
articles.body:
Question

I uploaded a new SSL certificate and it looks correct (right expiry date, active on my account), but Admin Center still shows a Replacement pending message. Why, and how do I clear it?

Answer

If multiple recent certificate uploads were initiated, each upload attempt can appear as its own pending entry, even if some of those attempts failed earlier or are still awaiting Zendesk approval. Once Zendesk approves the latest successful certificate upload, any older pending entries may still remain visible.

These older pending requests can be removed by clicking Cancel certificate for each pending entry. Doing so will not affect the currently active certificate, as long as you already have a valid approved certificate in place that covers all of your host-mapped addresses.

For example, if you uploaded a certificate 3 times and the 3rd attempt was the one that was successfully approved, the earlier 2 attempts may still appear as pending. Those 2 pending entries can be safely cancelled without impacting the active certificate.

articles.name: Can I hide or remove an attachment I accidentally sent to a customer in a ticket comment?
articles.title: Can I hide or remove an attachment I accidentally sent to a customer in a ticket comment?
articles.body:
Question

Can I hide or remove an attachment I accidentally sent to a customer in a ticket comment?

Answer

No. Once an attachment has been sent to a customer in a public ticket comment over email, it can’t be removed from the customer’s inbox by Zendesk.

If you redact the attachment in Zendesk, it is removed from Zendesk-controlled systems only. It is not removed from:

  • The email already delivered to the customer
  • The customer’s email provider, such as Gmail or Outlook
  • External platforms or third-party integrations where the file may already have been delivered

What you can do

If an attachment was sent by mistake:

  1. Redact the attachment in Zendesk to remove it from your account where supported. See Redacting ticket content.
  2. Contact the customer and ask them to disregard or delete the attachment.
  3. Review your attachment settings to help reduce future risk, such as using attachment expiration where available. See Allowing attachments in tickets.
Important: Redaction in Zendesk does not retract or delete emails that have already been sent outside Zendesk.

articles.name: What do the different automated resolution types mean in Automated resolutions dashboard?
articles.title: What do the different automated resolution types mean in Automated resolutions dashboard?
articles.body:
Question

What do the different automated resolution types mean in Automated resolutions dashboard?

Answer

Zendesk reporting may show several automated resolution types depending on which automation product or workflow resolved the customer interaction. These labels do not all refer to the same feature set.

Conversations

These are resolutions from your legacy AI agent (Answer Bot) on messaging channels like the Web Widget, mobile SDK, or third-party channels such as Facebook Messenger or WhatsApp where the end user's issue was resolved without agent involvement.

Auto-replies

These are resolutions where your legacy AI agent suggested help center articles over email or web form, and the customer either closed their request or engaged with the suggested article and did not reply again within 72 hours. For Web Widget (Classic), resolutions are counted when the customer views a suggested article preview or marks the issue solved within a 2-hour session.

Topic based triggers

These are resolutions from a Support trigger that automatically sends article recommendations based on ticket conditions (like subject or form field). It counts as resolved once the customer doesn't send another public reply within 72 hours.

Chat automation

These are resolutions from AI agents handling real-time chat conversations (for example, in the Web Widget or mobile SDK) where the AI agent resolved the issue without handing off to a human agent.

Ticket automation

These are resolutions from AI agents handling ticket-based (email/async) conversations, where the AI agent resolved the issue without a human agent needing to respond.

Voice automation

These are resolutions from AI agents handling voice conversations, where the AI agent resolved the caller's issue without transferring to a human agent.

ES AI Agents

These are resolutions generated by legacy AI agents - Essential usage.

Why don't I see all of these types on my dashboard?

The dashboard only shows types with usage during the selected period, so if you only use AI agents for chat, you'll just see "Chat automation" (and maybe "Conversations" or "Auto-replies" if legacy Answer Bot features are still active). An empty type simply means you haven't used that feature.

For more information, see Monitoring usage on the automated resolution platform.

Note: Because Zendesk automation offerings have evolved over time, these resolution types may reflect both legacy and current product experiences.

articles.name: Using tailored recommendations to automate manual tasks and optimize workflows in AI agents
articles.title: Using tailored recommendations to automate manual tasks and optimize workflows in AI agents
articles.body:
In the AI agents workspace, the Recommendations page shows you tailored recommendations for creating either a help center article or agenerative procedureto help automate workflows in your AI agent.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Use tailored AI agent recommendations to identify workflows you can automate by creating help center articles or generative procedures. Review each recommendation’s automation potential and rationale, then create it, save it for later, skip it, or mark it as done. Recommendations update weekly, and you can review saved, completed, and skipped items.

In the AI agents workspace, the Recommendations page shows you tailored recommendations for creating either a help center article or a generative procedure to help automate workflows in your AI agent.

Recommendations update every week, and change as your account data changes. Check the Recommendations page regularly to see new recommendations and determine whether any saved recommendations still apply.
Note: The Recommendations page appears for client admins and client editors, but not for client users. See AI agents roles.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Viewing all active recommendations for an AI agent
  • Viewing and processing a recommendation
  • Viewing saved, completed, and skipped recommendations

Viewing all active recommendations for an AI agent

You can access the recommendations for a specific AI agent from either the sidebar or the AI agent’s overview.

To access recommendations from the sidebar

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Optimize in the sidebar, then select Recommendations.

    The Recommendations page opens.

  3. (Optional) Click Filter and select either Articles or Procedures to filter the list by whether the recommendation involves creating a help center article or a generative procedure.

To access recommendations from an AI agent’s overview

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Optimize in the sidebar, then select Agent overview.
  3. Scroll down to the Recommendations section.

  4. Click View all.

    The Recommendations page opens.

Viewing and processing a recommendation

For any recommendation, you can view more details about why the system is suggesting it and what’s involved in implementing it. From there, you can decide whether you want to implement the recommendation, save it for later, or skip it altogether.

To view and process a recommendation

  1. On the Recommendations page, click the recommendation you want to view more details about.

    The Recommendation details panel opens.

  2. Review the details of the recommendation:
    • Automation potential: An estimated percentage of your tickets that could be automatically resolved using knowledge sources connected to an AI agent. This estimate is drawn from an analysis of your tickets by a specially tuned large language model (LLM) that assesses ticket topics for automatability, complexity, and agent effort, and then assigns an estimated score based on how automatable those tickets are likely to be.
    • Article or Procedure: An indication of whether the recommendation involves creating a help center article or a generative procedure.
    • Rationale: An explanation of why the recommendation is being suggested.
    • Last updated date: The date the recommendation was last evaluated by the system.
  3. Depending on how you want to handle the recommendation, do one of the following:
    • Generate an article or procedure from the recommendation.
    • Save the recommendation for later.
    • Skip the recommendation altogether.
    • Mark the recommendation as done.

Generate an article or procedure from a recommendation

If you want to implement a recommendation, you can create either a help center article or generative procedure, depending on what the recommendation is.

To implement a recommendation

  1. While viewing a recommendation’s details, click either Create article or Create procedure, depending on the type of recommendation.

    The system begins creating the article or procedure, and the AI-generated content appears when it is ready.

  2. If the recommendation was for an:
    • Article, the article opens as a draft in the article editor where you can review, edit, and publish, if you want.
    • Procedure, the use case is created and the procedure opens for you to review and edit. If you want to publish the procedure, click Publish procedure and the procedure is added to your list of procedures.
  3. In the Recommendations section, you can mark the recommendation as done if it is completed.

Saving a recommendation for later

If you want to implement a recommendation, but don’t have time right now, you can save it for later.

To save a recommendation for later

  • While viewing a recommendation’s details, click the drop-down arrow and select Save for later.

    Alternatively, on the Recommendations page, you can hover over the recommendation you want to save for later and click the Save for later icon.

    The recommendation is moved to the Saved tab on the Recommendations page.

Skipping a recommendation

If you don’t want to implement a recommendation at all, you can skip it.

To skip a recommendation

  1. While viewing a recommendation’s details, click Skip.

    Alternatively, on the Recommendations page, you can hover over the recommendation you want to skip, click the options menu (), and select Skip.

    A dialog appears.

  2. Under Why wasn’t this recommendation helpful?, select one of the following reasons for why you didn’t implement the recommendation:
    • Unclear rationale
    • I’ve already implemented this
    • I see this recommendation too often
    • It doesn’t apply to my business
    • Another reason
  3. (Optional) In Additional feedback, provide any additional comments about why you didn’t implement the recommendation.

  4. Click Submit feedback.

    Or, click Skip to skip the recommendation without providing feedback.

    In either case, the recommendation is moved to the Archived tab of the Recommendations archive.

Marking a recommendation as done

After you create an article or procedure from a recommendation, you can mark it as done so that it’s removed from the All recommendations tab of the Recommendations page.

Alternatively, you can indicate that a recommendation has been implemented without using the system-guided article or procedure creation process (for instance, if you manually created an article or procedure).

To mark a recommendation as done

  • While viewing a recommendation’s details, click the drop-down arrow and select Mark as done.

    The recommendation is moved to the Done tab of the Recommendations archive.

Viewing saved, completed, and skipped recommendations

After you save, complete, or skip a recommendation, you can still view its details for historical purposes:

  • Viewing saved recommendations
  • Viewing completed recommendations
  • Viewing skipped recommendations

Viewing saved recommendations

After you save a recommendation for later, you can view it on the Saved tab of the Recommendations page.

If necessary, you can move a saved recommendation back to the All recommendations tab.

To view and move a saved recommendation

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Optimize in the sidebar, then select Recommendations.
  3. Select the Saved tab.

    This tab shows all recommendations that have been saved for later.

How do I find recommendations for my AI agent, and who can view them?

In the AI agents workspace, select an AI agent, then choose Optimize > Recommendations, or choose Optimize > Agent overview and click View all in the Recommendations section. Client admins and client editors can see this page; client users cannot. You can filter recommendations by Articles or Procedures. Recommendations update weekly and can change as your account data changes.

What information can I see about a recommendation, and what does its automation potential mean?

Open a recommendation to see its automation potential estimate, whether it involves an article or procedure, the rationale, and the last updated date. Automation potential is the estimated percentage of your tickets that could be automatically resolved using knowledge sources connected to the AI agent. It is based on an analysis of ticket topics, automatability, complexity, and agent effort.

How do I create content from a recommendation and make it available to customers?

Open the recommendation and click Create article or Create procedure, as applicable. Review and edit the generated content, then click Save. The article or procedure is saved as a draft in its respective list. To make it live for customers, publish it, then mark the recommendation as done. You can also mark it done if you implemented it outside the guided creation process.

How can I set aside or dismiss a recommendation?

To set it aside, choose Save for later from the recommendation details menu or use the Save for later icon; it moves to the Saved tab. To dismiss it, click Skip or use the options menu. You can select a reason and optionally add feedback, or skip without feedback; dismissed recommendations move to the Archived tab.

Can I find a recommendation after I save, complete, or skip it, and can I restore it?

Saved recommendations are on the Saved tab, and you can return one to All recommendations by choosing Remove from Saved. Completed recommendations appear under the Done tab of View archive, and skipped recommendations appear under Archived. You can view their details, but completed and skipped recommendations cannot be moved back to the Recommendations page.
